title: Theorem
body_md: Let $\ell$ be a prime. Let $S_0$ be an integral scheme of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$ with function field $k$. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a finite type morphism with generic fiber $X_k$. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_k)$ be a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf with coefficients in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. There exists a dense open subscheme $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ and $M_0 \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_0/U_0)$ such that the restriction of $M_0$ to the generic fiber is isomorphic to $M$. If $U_0$ is geometrically unibranch, the extension to $U_0$ is unique up to unique isomorphism.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $S$ be the spectrum of the strict henselization of a discrete valuation ring essentially of finite type over a field. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $S$ and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{{\eta}})$ a geometrically semisimple arithmetic perverse sheaf on the generic fiber.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item The graded pieces of the monodromy filtration $\textnormal{Gr}^M_n(\Psi^{\textnormal{uni}}(M))$ are geometrically semisimple for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.
			\item Let $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a proper morphism of finite type $S$-schemes. The monodromy spectral sequence
			\[
			E_1^{pq} := {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\textnormal{Gr}_{-q}^M(\Psi^{\textnormal{uni}}(M)))) \Rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\Psi^{\textnormal{uni}}(M)))
			\]
			degenerates on the second page. Moreover, the filtration induced by the monodromy spectral sequence agrees with the monodromy filtration. 
		\end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a finitely presented morphism of qcqs schemes. We consider one of the following two coefficient rings $R$:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The ring $R$ is a complete Noetherian local ring. We assume the characteristic of $R/{\mathfrak{m}}$ is invertible on $Y$.
		\item The ring $R$ is $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ for a prime $\ell$ invertible on $Y$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Let $K, L \in \textnormal{D}_c^b(X, R)$ be constructible complexes of $R$-modules. There exists a finite constructible partition
	\[
	Y = \bigsqcup_{i = 1}^n Y_i
	\]
	such that all $1 \leq i \leq n$ satisfy: 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The pushforward $f_*(K|_{Y_i})$ is constructible over $Y_i$.
		\item The formation of the pushforward $f_*(K|_{Y_i})$ commutes with base change $Y' \rightarrow Y_i$.
		\item The complex $K|_{Y_i}$ is universally locally acyclic over $Y_{i}$.
		\item There exists an internal mapping object $\textnormal{Hom}(K|_{Y_i}, L|_{Y_i}) \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X_{Y_i}, R)$.
		\item The formation of the internal mapping object $\textnormal{Hom}(K|_{Y_i}, L|_{Y_i})$ commutes with base change $Y' \rightarrow Y_i$. 
	\end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{geomsimple_THM}
	Let $X$ be a geometrically connected geometrically unibranch  $k$-scheme. Let $F$ be a lisse geometrically semisimple $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf on $X$. There exists a finite separable extension $k'/k$, lisse geometrically irreducible $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves $F_1, \ldots, F_n$ on $X_{k'}$, and continuous $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representations $\rho_1, \ldots, \rho_n$ of the Galois group $G_{k'}$ of $k'$ such that
	\[
	F_{k'} \cong (F_1\otimes\rho_1)\oplus\ldots \oplus (F_n\otimes \rho_n).
	\]
	For all $1 \leq i \leq n$, we can choose $F_i$ so that the geometric and the arithmetic monodromy groups of $F_i$ agree.

label: conjaction_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{conjaction_LEM}
	Let $\rho\colon G \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}(V)$ be a continuous finite dimensional representation over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ of a profinite group $G$. Let $H \subseteq G$ be a normal closed subgroup. There exists an open subgroup $U \subseteq G$, such that the conjugation action of $U$  on the isomorphism classes of the irreducible subquotients of $\rho|_H$ is trivial.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By Jordan-Hölder, there is a finite number of trace functions $t_1, \ldots, t_n$ associated to the irreducible subquotients of $\rho|_H$. Note that any decomposition series of $\rho|_H$ descends to a finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ (see \cite[Lem.~4.3.7]{BhattSPE}). In particular, the trace functions $t_i$ take values in $K$ and are continuous. The group $G$ acts continuously on $H$ by conjugation. The conjugation action of $G$ induces a continuous action on $\textnormal{Hom}(H, K)$ in the compact-open topology. It preserves the finite set $\{t_1, \ldots, t_n\}$. The subspace $\{t_1, \ldots, t_n\}$ is finite and Hausdorff, hence discrete.  Therefore, the stabilizer of $t_i$ in $G$ is open. Since irreducible $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representations of $H$ are classified by their trace functions, this implies that the isomorphism class of each irreducible subquotient of $\rho|_H$ is stabilized by an open subgroup of $G$.

label: descentlocsys_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{descentlocsys_LEM}
	Let $X$ be a geometrically connected geometrically unibranch  $k$-scheme and $F$ an irreducible lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf on $X_{\overline{k}}$. Suppose 
	\[
	\sigma^*(F) \cong F
	\]
	for all $\sigma\in G_k$. There exists a finite separable extension $k'/k$ such that $F$ descends to a lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $F'$ on $X_{k'}$. We can choose $F'$ so that the geometric and the arithmetic monodromy group of $F'$ agree.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We have a short exact sequence
	\[
	0 \rightarrow \pi_1(X_{\overline{k}}) \rightarrow \pi_1(X) \rightarrow G_k \rightarrow 0.
	\]
	This short exact sequence splits after a finite separable extension $k'/k$. Proposition \ref{descentmonodromy_PROP} implies that after a finite separable extension $k''/k'$, the sheaf $F$  descends to a lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $F'$ on $X_{k''}$ such that the geometric and the arithmetic monodromy group of $F'$ agree.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma \ref{conjaction_LEM} implies that after a finite separable extension $k'/k$ the conjugation action of $\pi_1(X_{k'})$ on the isotypical components of $F_{\overline{k}}$ is trivial. In particular, we obtain a direct sum decomposition
	\[
	F_{k'} = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^n G_i
	\] 
	such that $G_i$ is geometrically isotypical for $1 \leq i \leq n$. Lemma \ref{descentlocsys_LEM} implies that there is a finite extension $k''/k'$ and a geometrically irreducible lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $F_i$ on $X_{k''}$  whose geometric and the arithmetic monodromy groups agree, and such that $G_i$ is geometrically $F_i$-isotypical. Define the $G_{k''}$-representation
	\[
	\rho_i := \textnormal{Hom}_{\pi_1(X_{\overline{k}})}(F_i, G_i).
	\]
	Then we have an isomorphism given by evaluation
	\[
	\rho_i\otimes F_i = G_i.
	\]
	Thus
	\[
	F_{k''} = (F_1\otimes \rho_1)\oplus \ldots \oplus (F_n\otimes \rho_n).
	\]

label: uniquenessmodels_REM
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{uniquenessmodels_REM}
	Models of schemes are unique up to finite field extensions. Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme. Let $X'$ and $X''$ be models of $X$ over fields $k_0 \subseteq k$ and $k_1 \subseteq k$. There exists a finite extension $k_2/k_0k_1$ such that $X'_{k_2} \cong X''_{k_2}$ by a limit argument (see \cite[Prop.~10.1]{milne2024descentalgebraicschemes}). In particular, a model over an algebraically closed field is unique up to isomorphism.
	
	Models of schemes are also unique up to finitely generated field extensions contained in the base-field. We consider schemes $X$, $X'$, and $X''$ as above. Then we have an isomorphism
	\[
	X'\times_{k_1} k \cong X''\times_{k_2}k.
	\]
	Since the schemes $X'$ and $X''$ are of finite type, there exists a finitely generated field extension $k_3/k_0k_1$ of $k_0k_1$ with $k_3 \subseteq k$ such that
	\[
	X'\times_{k_0}k_3 = X''\times_{k_1}k_3
	\]
	Thus we see that models of schemes are unique up to finitely generated field extensions. 
	
	A further limit argument implies that any scheme $X$ of finite type over a field $k$ admits a model over an arithmetic subfield $k_0 \subseteq k$.

label: arithmeticcomplex_DEF
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{arithmeticcomplex_DEF}
	Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme. A complex $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X)$ is called \textit{arithmetic} if there exists a model $X'$ of $X$ over an arithmetic field $k_0$ such that the following condition is satisifed. The model induces an $\textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_0)$-action on $X_{\overline{k}}$. The orbit $\sigma^*(K_{\overline{k}})$ for  $\sigma \in \textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_0)$ consists of finitely many isomorphism classes.

label: subquotientsarithmetic_THM
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that the perverse cohomology sheaves of $K$ are arithmetic because an isomorphism $\sigma^*(K) \xrightarrow{\sim} K$ induces isomorphisms
	\[
	\sigma^*({}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{n}(K)) \xrightarrow{\sim} {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{n}(K)
	\]
	for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ by $t$-exactness of $\sigma^*$. 
	
	We assume $K$ is perverse. Let $X'$ be a model over an arithmetic field $k_0$ such that the orbit of the isomorphism class $K_{\overline{k}}$ under the $\textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_0)$-action is finite. Let $\{M_1, \ldots, M_n\}$ be the orbit of the isomorphism class of $K_{\overline{k}}$. Let $\{N_1,\ldots, N_m\}$ be the isomorphism classes of irreducible subquotients of $M_1, \ldots, M_n$. Then $\textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_0)$ acts on the set $\{N_1, \ldots, N_m\}$ by the Jordan-Hölder theorem because the functors $\sigma^*$ are $t$-exact equivalences of categories for $\sigma \in \textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_0)$. In particular, the orbit of $N_i$ is finite for $1 \leq i \leq m$.

label: smoothbasechange_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{smoothbasechange_LEM}
	Let $k$ be a separably closed field and $X$ a $k$-scheme. Let $k'/k$ be a separably closed extension and $K, L \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X)$ complexes on $X$. The base change morphism
	\[
	\textnormal{Hom}(K, L) \rightarrow \textnormal{Hom}(K_{k'}, L_{k'})
	\]
	is an isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\alpha\colon X_{k'} \rightarrow X$ be the base change morphism. \cite[Prop.~9.5.5]{LeiFu} implies that the morphism
	\[
	\alpha^*(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)) \rightarrow \textnormal{Hom}(\alpha^*(K), \alpha^*(L)) 
	\]
	is an isomorphism. The natural morphism
	\[
	H^0(X, \textnormal{Hom}(K, L)) \rightarrow 	H^0(X_{k'}, \alpha^*(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L))) 
	\]
	is an isomorphism by smooth base change. Thus the composite
	\[
	\textnormal{Hom}(K, L) \rightarrow \textnormal{Hom}(\alpha^*(K), \alpha^*(L)) 
	\]
	is an isomorphism. This composite identifies with the morphism above.

label: lefschetzprinciple_LEM
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We can assume $k$ to be algebraically closed by base changing $k$ to $\overline{k}$. The uniqueness follows from Lemma \ref{smoothbasechange_LEM}.

	
	We construct a subfield $k_1 \subseteq k$ during the proof by repeatedly adjoining a finite number of elements of $k$ to $k_1$. We then say that we are enlarging $k_1$. We begin the argument with $k_1 := k_0$. 
	
	We assume the lemma is known when $K$ is a perverse sheaf. We now prove the lemma by induction on the number of non-zero perverse cohomology sheaves of $K$. In the base case we have $K = 0$, i.e. there is nothing to prove. Suppose $K$ has at least one non-zero perverse cohomology sheaf. Let $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ be the largest integer with ${}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{n}(K) \neq 0$. We have a distinguished triangle
	\[
	{{^\mathfrak{p}{\tau}^{\leq n - 1}}}(K) \rightarrow K \rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{n}(K)[-n] \xrightarrow[]{+}.
	\]
	We can enlarge $k_1$ such that the complexes ${{^\mathfrak{p}{\tau}^{\leq n - 1}}}(K)$ and ${}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{n}(K)$ admit models over ${\overline{k}_1}$ by the induction hypothesis and the assumption. By Lemma \ref{smoothbasechange_LEM}, the morphism
	\[
	{}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{n}(K)[-n] \rightarrow {{^\mathfrak{p}{\tau}^{\leq n - 1}}}(K)[1]
	\]
	descends to a morphism of models on $X'_{\overline{k}_1}$. Hence its cone admits a model on $X'_{\overline{k}_1}$. The cone is $K[1]$ hence $K$ admits a model on $X'_{\overline{k}_1}$.
	
	We assume the lemma is known when $K$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf. We can now prove the lemma for a perverse sheaf by induction on the length, similar to the first step.
	
	We treat the case when $K$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf. There exists a locally closed immersion $j\colon U \rightarrow X$ with $U$ irreducible and smooth such that $j^*(K)$ is lisse, concentrated in degree $-d$ for some integer $d \geq 0$, and $K = j_{!*}j^*(K)$. We can enlarge $k_1$ and assume the locally closed subset $j\colon U \rightarrow X$ admits a model 
	\[
	U' \rightarrow X'_{k_1}
	\]
	over $k_1$. Note that $U'$ is geometrically irreducible and smooth because $U$ is irreducible and smooth and $k$ is algebraically closed.
	
	Assume, after enlarging $k_1$, that $j^*(K)$ admits a model on $U'_{\overline{k}_1}$. The complex $K$ admits a model on $X'_{\overline{k}_1}$, since intermediate extension commutes with base change. Therefore, it is sufficient if we construct a model for $j^*(K)$ on $U_{\overline{k}_1}$ after enlarging $k_1$. We can write $j^*(K) = F[d]$ for a lisse sheaf $F$ on $U$. In particular, it is sufficient to construct a model of $F$ on $U'_{\overline{k}_1}$ after an enlargement of $k_1$.  
	
	There exists a finite Galois cover $q\colon V \rightarrow U$ such that $q^*(F)$ has pro-$\ell$-monodromy (i.e. the image of the fundamental group $\pi_1(V)$ in $\textnormal{GL}(F)$ is a pro-$\ell$ group). We can enlarge $k_1$ and assume $q$ descends to a finite Galois cover $V' \rightarrow U'$ over $k_1$. Assume $q^*(F)$ admits a model on $V'_{\overline{k}_1}$.  The base change morphism
	\[
	\pi_1(U) \rightarrow \pi_1(U'_{{\overline{k}_1}})
	\]
	is surjective because $\overline{k}_1$ is separably closed. Thus any direct factor of $q_*q^*(F)$ admits a model on $U'_{\overline{k}_1}$. In particular, $F$ admits a model over $\overline{k}_1$ because $F$ is a direct factor of $q_*q^*(F)$ by the projection formula. Thus it is sufficient if we construct a model of $q^*(F)$ on $V'_{\overline{k}_1}$.
	
	The base change morphism
	\[
	\pi_1^{\ell}(V_{\overline{k}}) \rightarrow \pi_1^{\ell}(V'_{{\overline{k}_1}})
	\]
	on pro-$\ell$ fundamental groups is an isomorphism by \cite[Cor.~4.5]{orgogozoFundamentalGroup}. Thus $q^*(F)$ admits a model over $\overline{k}_1$.

label: modelsIrr_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{modelsIrr_THM}
	Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X)$ be a geometrically irreducible arithmetic perverse sheaf on $X$. For a model $X'$ of $X$ over a field $k_0 \subseteq k$, there exists a finitely generated field extension $k_1/k_0$ with $k_1 \subseteq\overline{k}$ and a one-dimensional character $\chi$ of the Galois group of $k_1k$ such that $M_{k_1k}\otimes \chi$ admits a model on $X'_{k_1}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We construct $k_1$ by enlarging the field during the proof as in Lemma \ref{lefschetzprinciple_LEM}. By Remark \ref{independence_RMK}, we can assume the action of $\textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_1)$ has a finite orbit when acting on the isomorphism class of $M$ by taking a finitely generated extension $k_1/k_0$. By Lemma \ref{lefschetzprinciple_LEM}, we can enlarge $k_1$ and assume $M$ descends to a model $M'_{\overline{k}_1}$ on $X'_{\overline{k}_1}$.
	
	After a finite extension of $k_1$, we can assume there exists an immersion $j\colon U \rightarrow X'_{k_1}$ with $U$ smooth and geometrically connected, $M_{k_1k} = j_{!*}(j^*(M_{k_1k}))$, and $j^*(M_{k_1k})$ is lisse. Since the intermediate extension commutes with base change, we can replace $X$ by $U$ and assume $M$, and hence $M'_{\overline{k}_1}$, are lisse.
	
	The action of $\textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_1)$ on the isomorphism class of $M$ factors through the Galois group $G_{k_1}$ of $k_1$. Therefore, the action of $G_{k_1}$ has a finite orbit when acting on the isomorphism class of $M'_{\overline{k}_1}$ because the restriction morphism
	\[
	\textnormal{Aut}(\overline{k}/k_1) \rightarrow G_{k_1}
	\] 
	is surjective. An argument with trace functions, similar to the one in Lemma \ref{conjaction_LEM}, implies that the stabilizer in $G_{k_1}$ of $M$ is closed and hence open (see also \cite[Cor.~5.4]{zockmasterthesis}). Thus, after passing to a finite (separable) extension of $k_1$, Lemma \ref{descentlocsys_LEM} implies that $M'_{\overline{k}_1}$ descends to a model $M'$ on $X_{k_1}$. The space 
	\[
	\chi := \textnormal{Hom}(M'_{\overline{k}}, M_{\overline{k}})
	\] 
	is one-dimensional and comes with a continuous action by the group $G_{k_1k}$. We have an isomorphism given by evaluation
	\[
	M'_{k_1k}\otimes\chi = M_{k_1k}.
	\]
	Thus $M'$ is a model of $M_{k_1k}\otimes\chi^\vee$ on $X'_{k_1}$.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{models_COR}
	Let $k$ be a separably closed field and $X$ a  $k$-scheme. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X)$ be an arithmetic semisimple complex. The complex $K$ admits a model over an arithmetic field.

title: Proof
body_md: Because $K$ is semisimple and the irreducible factors are arithmetic by Theorem \ref{subquotientsarithmetic_THM}, we can assume $K$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf. The sheaf $K$ is then geometrically irreducible. This case is treated by Theorem \ref{modelsIrr_THM}.

label: geomsimpleperverse_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{geomsimpleperverse_THM}
	Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X)$ be a geometrically semisimple perverse sheaf on $X$. There exists a finite separable extension $k'/k$, geometrically irreducible perverse sheaves $M_1, \ldots, M_n \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{k'})$, and continuous $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representations $\rho_1, \ldots, \rho_n$ of the Galois group of $k$ such that
	\[
	M_{k'} = (M_1\otimes\rho_1) \oplus \ldots \oplus (M_n\otimes\rho_n).
	\]
	If $M$ is arithmetic, then $M_i$ is arithmetic for $1\leq i \leq n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Z_1, \ldots, Z_n \subseteq X_{\overline{k}}$ be the supports of the irreducible subquotients of $M_{\overline{k}}$. There exists a finite separable extension $k'/k$ such that the closed subsets come from base change by geometrically irreducible closed subsets $Z_i \subseteq X_{k'}$. For all closed immersions $i\colon Z \rightarrow X_{k'}$ the natural map induces an isomorphism
	\[
	{}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{0}(i^!(M)) \rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{0}(i^*(M))
	\]
	because it induces an isomorphism after base change to $X_{\overline{k}}$ by geometric semisimplicity. 
	In particular, we obtain a decomposition
	\[
	M_{k'} = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^n N_i
	\]
	with perverse sheaves $N_i \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{k'})$ whose irreducible subquotients have support $Z_i$. Let $1 \leq i \leq n$. There is a dense open immersion $j\colon U_i \rightarrow Z_i$ such that $M_i$ is lisse over $U_i$, the scheme $U_i$ is geometrically unibranch, and we have 
	\[
	M'_i = j_{!*}j^*(N_i).
	\] 
	For $j^*(N_i)$, the required decomposition was constructed in Theorem \ref{geomsimple_THM}.
	
	Note that $(M_i)_{\overline{k}}$ are irreducible subquotients of $M_{\overline{k}}$, hence they are arithmetic by Theorem \ref{subquotientsarithmetic_THM}.

label: intermed_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{intermed_LEM}
		Let $S_0$ be an irreducible qcqs scheme and $X_0$ an $S_0$-scheme. Let $j\colon V_0 \rightarrow X_0$ be an immersion and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(V_0/S_0)$. There exists a constructible dense open subscheme $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ and $N \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_{U_0}/U_0)$ such that $N_x = j_{!*}(M_x)$ for all $x \in U_0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By generic base change (see Theorem \ref{genbc_THM}), there exists a constructible dense open subscheme $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ so that $j_*(M)$ is constructible over $U_0$. We define $N \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{U_0}/U_0)$ to be the relative perverse image of the morphism 
		\[
		{}^{{\mathfrak{p}}/U_0} \mathscr{H}^0(j_! M) \rightarrow {}^{{\mathfrak{p}}/U_0} \mathscr{H}^0(j_* M)
		\]
		By Theorem \ref{genbc_THM}, we can shrink $U_0$ so that $j_*(M)$ commutes with base change over $U_0$. For all $x \in U_0$, this implies that the complex $N_x$ coincides with $j_{!*}(M_x)$, since restriction to a fiber induces an exact functor from the relatively perverse category to the absolutely perverse category on the fiber. We can shrink $U_0$ again so that $N$ is ULA over $U_0$ by Theorem \ref{genula_THM}.

label: relreduced_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{relreduced_LEM}
		Let $S_0$ be an integral qcqs scheme with function field $k$. Let $X_0$ be an $S_0$-scheme. We assume the reduced generic geometric fiber $(X_{\overline{k}})^{\textnormal{red}}$ is smooth over $\overline{k}$. There exists a universal homeomorphism $F\colon S_0 \rightarrow S_0$ and a dense open constructible subscheme $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that 
		\[
		(X_0\times_{S_0, F}U_0)^{\textnormal{red}} \rightarrow U_0
		\]
		is smooth.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If the characteristic of $k$ is zero, there is nothing to prove. Suppose the characteristic of $k$ is $p > 0$. There exists $n \geq 1$ such that $(X_{k^{p^{-n}}})^{\textnormal{red}}$ is geometrically reduced over $k^{p^{-n}}$. Therefore, $(X_{k^{p^{-n}}})^{\textnormal{red}}$ is smooth over $k^{p^{-n}}$. The $n$-fold Frobenius is a universal homeomorphism
		\[
		F\colon S_0 \rightarrow S_0
		\]
		which induces the extension $k^{p^{-n}}/k$ at the generic point.  In particular, the generic fiber of the morphism
		\[
		(X_0\times_{F, S_0}S_0)^{\textnormal{red}} \rightarrow S_0
		\]
		is smooth. Since this morphism is finitely presented, it is smooth over a constructible dense open subscheme of $S_0$.

label: filtration_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{filtration_THM}
		Let $S_0$ be a topologically Noetherian integral geometrically unibranch scheme with function field $k$. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a morphism of finite type and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_0/S_0)$ a relatively perverse sheaf over $S_0$. We assume the irreducible subquotients of $M_{k}$ have geometrically irreducible support.  There is a dense open subscheme $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ and relatively perverse sheaves $M_i \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_{U_0}/U_0)$ for $0 \leq i \leq n$ which fit into a filtration
		\[
		0 = M_0 \subset M_1 \subset \ldots M_{n - 1} \subset M_n = M_{U_0}.
		\]
		Moreover, we have a closed subset $Z_i \subseteq X_{U_0}$ and a dense open subscheme $V_i \subseteq Z_i$ for all $1\leq i \leq n$. The following properties are satisfied:
		\begin{enumerate}[]
			\item The generic fiber $(M_i/M_{i - 1})_k$ is irreducible.
			\item The morphism $Z_i \rightarrow U_0$ has geometrically irreducible fibers. 
			\item The morphism $V_i \rightarrow U_0$ has geometrically connected fibers. The reduced geometric fibers of $V_i \rightarrow U_0$ are smooth.
                                                                                                                                                    
			\item The restriction $(M_i/M_{i - 1})|_{V_i}$ is lisse.
			\item  The image of $\pi_1(V_{i, \overline{x}})$ in $\mathbf{GL}((M_i/M_{i -1})_{\overline{x}})$ does not depend on the geometric point $\overline{x} \rightarrow U_0$ up to conjugacy (see Definition \ref{conjugate_DEF}). 
			\item Denote by $j\colon V_i \rightarrow Z_i$ the inclusion. Let $x \in U_0$ be a point. We have
			\[
			j_{!*}(j^*((M_i/M_{i - 1})_x)) = (M_i/M_{i - 1})_x.
			\]
		\end{enumerate}

title: Proof
body_md:
Over the course  of the argument, we repeatedly shrink $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ without changing notation. By Theorem \ref{genula_THM}, we can shrink $S_0$ to a dense open subset $U_0\subseteq S_0$ so that $M$ is universally locally acyclic over $U_0$ by Theorem \ref{genula_THM}. By \cite[Thm.~1.10]{hansen2023relativeperversity}, we can lift a decomposition series of $M_k$ to a decomposition series 
		\[
		0 = M_0 \subset M_1 \subset \ldots \subset M_{n - 1} \subset M_n = M|_{U_0}
		\]
		of relatively perverse sheaves $M_i \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_0/U_0, \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)$. 
		
		This filtration reproduces a decomposition series on the generic fiber by construction, thus (1) is satisfied.
		
		Let $1 \leq i \leq n$. Define $Z_i$ to be the support of the quotient $M_i/M_{i - 1}$. Because the support of the generic fiber of $M_i/M_{i - 1}$ is geometrically irreducible by assumption, the support $Z_i$ is geometrically irreducible over the generic fiber. We can shrink $U_0$, so that $Z_i$ has geometrically irreducible fibers over $U_0$. Thus we obtain property (2). 
		
		There is a dense open subset $j_i\colon V_i \rightarrow Z_i$, such that $((V_i)_{\overline{k}})^{\textnormal{red}}$ is smooth, irreducible, and $M_i/M_{i - 1}$  is lisse over $V_i$. Thus we obtain (3) and (4). In particular, by shrinking $U_0$, the reduced geometric fibers of $V_i$ over $U_0$ are smooth and connected over $U_0$ by Lemma \ref{relreduced_LEM}.	In particular, by shrinking $U_0$, Lemma \ref{relreduced_LEM} allows us to assume there is a universal homeomorphism $U_0' \rightarrow U_0$ such that 
		\[
		(X_{U_0'})^{\textnormal{red}} \rightarrow U_0'
		\]
		is smooth. Therefore, Theorem \ref{specializationmonodromy_THM} applies to the fibers of this morphism. This implies we can shrink $U_0'$ so that the image of the fundamental group does not depend on the geometric fiber over $U_0'$ up to conjugacy. In particular, we can shrink $U_0$ so that the image of the fundamental group does not depend on the chosen geometric fiber over $U_0$. Therefore, property (5) is satisifed.
		
		By shrinking $U_0$, Lemma \ref{intermed_LEM} permits us to assume that there are relatively perverse universally locally acyclic sheaves $N_i \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_{U_0}/U_0, \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)$ such that $N_{i, x}$ is isomorphic to the intermediate extension $j_{i!*}((M_i/M_{i - 1})_x)$ for all $1 \leq i \leq n$. Since both $(M_i/M_{i -1})_k$ and $N_i$ are univerally locally acyclic and isomorphic to $j_{i!*}((M_i/M_{i - 1})_k)$ on the generic fiber,  \cite[Thm.~1.10]{hansen2023relativeperversity} shows that there is an isomorphism
		\[
		N_i \cong M_i/M_{i - 1}.
		\]  
		In particular, the fibers $(M_i/M_{i - 1})_x$ are intermediate extensions along the immersion $V_{i, x} \rightarrow Z_{i, x}$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $X_0$ be a connected Noetherian regular scheme with function field $k$ and $D_0 \subset X_0$ an irreducible divisor on $X_0$ with generic point $x \in X_0$. Let $k'$ be the fraction field of the strict henselization of $X_0$ at $x$.  Let $F$ be a representation of the Galois group of $k$ with coefficients in $\mathcal{O}$. We say $F$ is \textit{unramified along $D_0$}, if the Galois group $G_{k'}$ (the inertia) acts trivially on $F$. We say $F$ is \textit{unramified} if it is unramified along all irreducible divisors on $X_0$. We say it is \textit{generically unramified} if it is unramified at almost all divisors in $X_0$, i.e. if it ramifies only at finitely many irreducible divisors.

label: pickup_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{pickup_LEM}
	Let $S_0$ be the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring and $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ a smooth finite type morphism with connected fibers. Suppose we are given a section $s\colon S_0' \rightarrow X_0$ on a surjective etale neighborhood $S_0'\rightarrow S_0$. Let $F$ be lisse $\mathcal{O}$-sheaf on the generic fiber such that $s^*(F)$ is unramified and $F\otimes \mathcal{O}/\lambda\mathcal{O}$ is unramified along the special fiber. Then $F$ is unramified along the special fiber of $\pi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $T_0$ be the strict henselization of $X_0$ at the image of the closed point of $S_0$ along the section $s$. The special fiber is a connected regular Cartier divisor on $X_0$. In particular, the preimage $D_0 \subset T_0$ is a regular Cartier divisor on $T_0$. Thus $D_0$ is connected and regular. We denote by $\pi_1^t(T_0)$ the fundamental group of finite etale covers of $T_0 - D_0$ tamely ramified along $D_0$.
	
	Because $F\otimes\mathcal{O}/\lambda\mathcal{O}$ is unramified along the special fiber, the local system $F\otimes \mathcal{O}/\lambda\mathcal{O}$ extends to a local system on $X_0$ by Lemma \ref{unramifiedext_LEM}. Any local system on $T_0$ is trivial because it is a strictly henselian local ring.  Thus $F\otimes\mathcal{O}/\lambda\mathcal{O}$ restricted $T_0 - D_0$ is trivial because it extends to a local system on $T_0$. This implies that the image of the morphism
	\[
	\pi_1(T_0 - D_0) \rightarrow \textnormal{GL}(F_{\overline{k}})
	\]
	is a pro-$\ell$-group because it is trivial mod $\lambda$ (where $k$ is the function field of $S_0$). Note that the kernel of the morphism
	\[
	\pi_1(T_0 - D_0) \rightarrow \pi_1^t(T_0)
	\]
	admits no finite quotients of order co-prime to residual characteristic of the generic point of $D_0$. We have assumed $\ell$ to be invertible, which implies that the residual characteristic of the generic point of $D_0$ is not $\ell$. Now we obtain that the Galois group of the function field of $T_0$ acts through $\pi_1^t(T_0)$ on $F$.
	
	Let $T$ be the strict henselization of the generic point of $D_0$ in $X_0$ and $\Tilde{S}_0$ the strict henselization of $S_0$. The section lifts to a section $\tilde{s}\colon \Tilde{S}_0 \rightarrow T_0$, hence we have a diagram	
	\[
	                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
	\begin{tikzcd}
		\pi_1^t(T) \arrow[r] & {\pi_1^t(T_0)} \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & \pi_1^t(\Tilde{S}_0) \arrow[l, "\Tilde{s}"', bend right=30] \\
		& \textnormal{GL}(F_{\overline{k}})                                 &                                            
	\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	By Abhyankar's Lemma, see \cite[Exp.~XII,~Cor.~5.3]{SGA1}, all arrows in the first row of this diagram are isomorphisms. In particular, to prove the action of the Galois group of the generic point of $T$ on $F$ is trivial, it is sufficient to prove the action of the generic point of $\Tilde{S}_0$ on $s^*(F)$ is trivial. This is satisfied by assumption.

title: Proof

label: bcnearbycycles_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{bcnearbycycles_LEM}
	For almost all points of codimension one $x \in S_0$, the nearby cycles $\Psi_x(F)$ are lisse, irreducible, and the natural base change morphism
	\[
	s^*(\Psi_x(F)) \xrightarrow{\sim} \Psi_x(s^*(F))
	\]
	is an isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $N \geq 1$. By Lemma \ref{spreadsheaves_LEM}, there exists $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that $F_n$ extends to a local system on $X_{U_0}$ for all $1 \leq n \leq N$. We denote the extended local system by $F_n$ as well.
	
	The smooth base change theorem implies that the specialization map
	\[
	i_x^*(F_1) \rightarrow \Psi_x(F_1)
	\]
	and
	\[
	i_x^*(s^*(F_1)) \rightarrow \Psi_x^*(s^*(F_1))
	\]
	are isomorphisms for all codimension one points $x \in U_0$. Note that $i_x^*(F_1)$ is a local system, hence $\Psi_x(F_1)$ is a local system. This implies $\Psi_x(F')$ is a lisse sheaf, hence $\Psi_x(F)$ is a lisse sheaf (see \cite[Lem.~6.6.8]{BhattSPE})
	
	We have a commutative diagram
	\[
	                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
	\begin{tikzcd}
		s^*(i_x^*(F_1)) \arrow[r] \arrow[d, equal] & s^*(\Psi_x(F_1)) \arrow[d] \\
		i_x^*(s^*(F_1)) \arrow[r]         & \Psi_x(s^*(F_1))          
	\end{tikzcd}
	\]
	In particular, the base change $s^*(\Psi_x(F_1)) \rightarrow \Psi_x(s^*(F_1))$ is an isomorphism for all codimension one points $x \in U_0$. Nakayama's Lemma shows that
	\[
	s^*(\Psi_x(F)) \rightarrow \Psi_x(s^*(F))
	\]
	is an isomorphism for all codimension one points $x \in U_0$ (because the morphism is an isomorphism after taking the derived tensor product with $\mathcal{O}/\lambda$).
	
	To prove that the nearby cycles are irreducible we prove that the geometric monodromy of $F$ is conjugate to the monodromy of $\Psi_x(F)$ (see Definition \ref{conjugate_DEF}) at almost all codimension one points $x \in U_0$. Here, by (geometric) monodromy we mean the image of the (geometric) fundamental group in the general linear group of a fiber of $F$. Let $x \in U_0$ be a codimension one point. There exists a morphism $S \rightarrow S_0$ from the spectrum of an aic valuation ring of rank one $S$ to $S_0$ mapping the generic point to the generic point of $S_0$ and the special point to $y$. Let $j\colon X_{\eta} \rightarrow X_S$ be the inclusion of the generic fiber. We have
	\[
	j_*j^*(F_1) = F_1,
	\]
	by smooth base change.  Hence $j_*(F)$ is a lisse sheaf. We have a diagram on fundamental groups 
	\[
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
	\begin{tikzcd}
		& \pi_1^{}(X_{\overline{x}}) \arrow[d] &              \\
		\pi_1^{}(X_\eta) \arrow[r, two heads] & \pi_1(X_S) \arrow[r]             & \textnormal{GL}(j_*(F))
	\end{tikzcd}.
	\]
	by Lemma \ref{fundgroupsurjects_LEM} and Psoposition \ref{topnot_PROP}. Therefore, the monodromy of $\Psi_x(F)$ is conjugate to a subgroup of the geometric monodromy of $F$. 
	
	We can now argue as in the proof of Theorem \ref{specializationmonodromy_THM}, i.e. as in \cite[Thm.~8.18.2]{KatzESDE}, to show that for almost all codimension one points $x \in U_0$ the monodromy of $\Psi_x(F)$ is conjugate to the geometric monodromy of $F$. In particular, $\Psi_x(F)$ is irreducible for almost all codimension one points $x \in U_0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{bcnearbycycles_LEM}, the inertia acts by scalars on $\Psi_x(F)$ at almost all $x \in S_0$ of codimension one. The base change in Lemma \ref{bcnearbycycles_LEM} is equivariant for the inertia action. Thus the inertia acts by scalars on $s^*(F)$ at almost all points $x \in S_0$ of codimension 1. The character
	\[
	\textnormal{det}(s^*(F))
	\] 
	is generically unramified by assumption. Hence the inertia groups at almost all points $x \in S_0$ of codimension 1 act by multiplication by roots of unity on $s^*(F)$ of order bounded by the rank of $F$. There exists $N \geq 1$ such that the roots of unity of order bounded by the rank of $F$ inject into $(\mathcal{O}/\lambda^N\mathcal{O})^*$. By Lemma \ref{spreadsheaves_LEM}, we can find a dense open subset $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that $F_N$ extends to a local system over $X_{U_0}$. Thus the Galois representation $s^*(F)$ is generically unramified on $S_0$. We obtain the extension by Theorem \ref{extensionpre_THM}.

label: charactersunr_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md: \label{charactersunr_LEM}Suppose $S_0$ is arithmetic. Let $\chi \colon G_k \rightarrow \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^*$ be a continuous character. The character $\chi$ is generically unramified on $S_0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We can assume, by taking the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$ in a sufficiently large extension of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$, that the character factors through a character $\chi'\colon G_k \rightarrow \mathcal{O}^*$. The group $\mathcal{O}^*$ is a finitely generated pro-finite abelian group. In particular, it has a finite torsion part $F$ and there is a splitting
	\[
	\mathcal{O}^* = T\times F
	\]
	with a torsion-free profinite abelian group $F$ (a free $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-module of finite rank) and a finite group $T$. We denote by $\chi'_{\textnormal{fin}}\colon  G_k \rightarrow T$ the finite part of $\chi'$. Let $x \in S_0$ be a codimension $1$ point. By the quasi-unipotent monodromy theorem (see Proposition \ref{qunimon_PROP}), the action on $\chi$ by the inertia group at $x$ is finite. In particular, the character $\chi$ is unramified at $x$ if and only if $\chi'_{\textnormal{fin}}$ is unramified at $x$.
	
	Since the character $\chi_{\textnormal{fin}}$ has finite monodromy, it is generically unramified. Thus $\chi$ is generically unramified.

Hence we can assume $S_0$ is regular by passing to a dense open subscheme. The required section over an etale neighborhood of $S_0$ exists by \cite[Cor.~17.16.3~(ii)]{EGA4}. label: extension_THM
title: Theorem
body_md: \label{extension_THM} Let $S_0$ be a connected Noetherian regular scheme with function field $k$. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a finite type morphism and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_k)$ a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf on the generic fiber of this morphism. There exists a connected dominant etale neighborhood $S_0' \rightarrow S_0$ with function field $k'$, a character $\chi$ of the Galois group of $k'$, and a relatively perverse universally locally acylic sheaf $M_0 \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_0'/S_0')$ such that the generic fiber of $M_0$ is isomorphic to $M_{k'}\otimes\chi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
There is an immersion $j\colon V_k \rightarrow X_k$ by a reduced scheme $V_{k}$, such that $(V_{\overline{k}})^{\textnormal{red}}$ is connected and smooth of dimension $d$ and a lisse, geometrically $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $F$ on $V_k$ such that $M = j_{!*}(F[d])$.  The locally closed subscheme $V_k$ is geometrically connected because $M$ is geometrically irreducible. The subscheme $V_{k}$ spreads out to a locally closed subscheme $V_0 \subseteq X_0$ by a limit argument. By Lemma \ref{relreduced_LEM}, there exists a universal homeomorphism $F\colon S_0 \rightarrow S_0$ such that $(V_0\times_{F, S_0}S_0)^{\textnormal{red}}$ is generically smooth over $S_0$. The topological invariance of the proetale site (see \cite[Lem.~5.4.2]{BhattSPE}) allows us to base change along $F$ and pass to the reduced closed subscheme. Thus we may assume $V_0 \rightarrow S_0$ is smooth. By shrinking $S_0$ further, we can asssume $V_0 \rightarrow S_0$ has geometrically connected fibers because the generic fiber is geometrically connected.
	
	Because $V_0 \rightarrow S_0$ is smooth, \cite[Cor.~17.16.3~(ii)]{EGA4} shows that there exists an irreducible dominant etale neighborhood $S_0' \rightarrow S_0$ with a section $s\colon S_0' \rightarrow V_{S_0'}$. Let $k'$ be the function field of $S_0'$. Let $n$ be the rank of $F$. There exists a finite separable extension $k''/k'$ and a character $\chi$ of the Galois group of $k''$ such that 
	\[
	\chi^{-n} = s^*\textnormal{det}(F).
	\]
	This implies
	\[
	s^*\textnormal{det}(F\otimes\chi) = 1.
	\]
	Since the extension $k''/k'$ is separable, a limit argument implies that there exists a dominant etale neighborhood $S_0'' \rightarrow S_0'$ inducing the extension $k''/k'$ on function fields. Since $S_0'' \rightarrow S_0'$ is etale and $S_0'$ is regular, the scheme $S_0''$ is regular. Therefore, Theorem \ref{simpson_THM} shows, after shrinking $S_0''$, that $F\otimes\chi$ extends to a lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf on $X_0''$. By Lemma \ref{intermed_LEM}, we can shrink $S_0''$ further and obtain $M_0 \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_0''/S_0'')$ whose generic fiber is isomorphic to $M_{k''}\otimes\chi$.

label: geomdvr_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{geomdvr_LEM}
	Let $S$ be a discrete valuation ring essentially of finite type over a field $k_0$. There exists a finitely generated extension $k_1/k_0$, a regular geometrically connected curve $C$ over $k_1$, and a closed point $0 \in C$ such that there exists an isomorphism
	\[
	S \cong \mathcal{O}_{C,0}. 
	\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition, we can find a normal domain $R$ of finite type over $k_0$ and a prime ideal ${\mathfrak{p}} \subset R$ of height one with $R_{\mathfrak{p}} = S$. After localizing $R$, we may assume there is $\pi \in R$ such that ${\mathfrak{p}} = (\pi)$. Let ${\mathfrak{m}} \subset R$ be a maximal ideal with ${\mathfrak{p}} \subset {\mathfrak{m}}$, then we may find a system of parameters $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in {\mathfrak{m}}$ with $x_1 = \pi$. We then consider the morphism
	\[
	k_0[x_1, \ldots,x_n] \rightarrow R.
	\]
We consider the prime ideal ${\mathfrak{q}} := (x_1) \subset k_0[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$. Then we obtain a quasi-finite morphism
\[
k_0[x_1, \ldots, x_n]_{\mathfrak{q}} \rightarrow R_{\mathfrak{p}}
\]
because ${\mathfrak{p}}$ is the only prime ideal lying over ${\mathfrak{q}}$ by assumption. We have
\[
k_0[x_1, \ldots, x_n]_{{\mathfrak{q}}} = k_0(x_2, \ldots,x_n)[x_1]_{(x_1)}.
\]
Since $R_{\mathfrak{p}}$ is quasi-finite over this local ring, we see that it is also the localization of a normal curve by Zariski's main theorem. We can then normalize the field $k_0(x_2, \ldots,x_n)$ in $R_{\mathfrak{p}}$ to obtain a geometrically connected regular curve over a field finitely generated over $k_0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma \ref{geomdvr_LEM} implies $S$ is the strict henselization of the local ring of an affine regular geometrically connected curve $C$ over a field $k$ at a point $0 \in C$. We may write $k = \varinjlim k_i$ as the filtered union over all arithmetic subfields $k_i \subseteq k$. By passing to a subsystem, this permits us to write
	\[
	C = \varprojlim C_i
	\]
	as the cofiltered limit of geometrically connected regular affine curves $C_i$ over $k_i$ with distinguished points $0 \in C$. For each $i \in I$, we may write
	\[
	\textnormal{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_{C_i, 0}^{\textnormal{sh}}) = \varprojlim S_{i, j} 
	\]
	as the cofiltered limit over all connected affine etale neighborhoods $S_{i, j} \rightarrow C_i$ of $0$. Since this limit is functorial and the strict henselization commutes with filtered colimits (see \cite[Prop.~2.8.19,~(ii)]{LeiFu}), we obtain
	\[
	S = \varprojlim_{i, j} S_{i, j}.
	\] 
	Since we have $\pi \in \Gamma(S, \mathcal{O}_S)$, we may assume $\pi \in \Gamma(S_{i, j}, \mathcal{O}_{S_{i, j}})$ by passing to a subsystem. Thus we obtain the claim.

label: morphismzero_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{morphismzero_LEM}
		Let $S_0$ be an integral qcqs scheme with function field $k$. Let $X_0$ be an $S_0$-scheme and $K, L \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X_0)$ complexes admitting a morphism $K \rightarrow L$. The morphism $K_{\overline{k}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{k}}$ is zero if and only if there exists a dense subset $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that $K_{\overline{x}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{x}}$ is zero for all points $x \in U_0$. Moreover, if $K_{\overline{k}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{k}}$ vanishes, there exists a dense open subset $V_0 \subseteq X_0$ such that $K_{\overline{x}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{x}}$ vanishes for all $x \in V_0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem \ref{genbc_THM} and Theorem \ref{genbchom_THM}, there exists a dense open subscheme $V_0 \subseteq Y_0$ such that
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item The complex $\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)$ is constructible over $V_0$. 
			\item The formation of $\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)$ commutes with base change $Y \rightarrow V_0$.
			\item The formation of the pushforward $\pi_{*}(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L))$ commutes with base change $Y \rightarrow V_0$.
			\item The complex $\pi_*(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L))$ is lisse over $V_0$. 
		\end{enumerate}
		For all points $x \in V_0$, the specialization morphism of $\pi_{*}(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L))$ induces an isomorphism
		\[
		\textnormal{Hom}_{\textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X_{\overline{x}})}(K_{\overline{x}}, L_{\overline{x}})  \rightarrow \textnormal{Hom}_{\textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X_{\overline{k}})}(K_{\overline{k}}, L_{\overline{k}})  
		\]
		This isomorphism maps the morphism $K_{\overline{x}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{x}}$ to the morphism $L_{\overline{k}} \rightarrow K_{\overline{k}}$. 
		
		In particular, if $K_{\overline{k}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{k}}$ is zero, there exists the dense open subset $U_0 := V_0$ such that the fiber of the  morphism is zero over all closed points in $V_0$. 
		
		On the other hand, suppose we are given a dense subset $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that $K_{\overline{x}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{x}}$ is zero over all closed points $x \in U_0$. The subset $U_0\cap V_0 \subseteq S_0$ is non-empty, so we may choose $y \in U_0\cap V_0$. The morphism $K_{\overline{y}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{y}}$ is zero by assumption, so we can evaluate the specialization map to show  $K_{\overline{k}} \rightarrow L_{\overline{k}}$ is zero.

title: Corollary
body_md:

label: critsemisimpleperv_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{critsemisimpleperv_LEM}
		Let $S_0$ be an integral geometrically unibranch topologically Noetherian scheme with function field $k$. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a morphism of finite type. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_0/S_0)$. Then $M_{\overline{k}}$ is semisimple if and only if there is a dense subset $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that for all $x \in U_0$ the restriction to the geometric fiber $M_{\overline{x}}$ is semisimple. Moreover, if the the generic fiber $M_{\overline{k}}$ is semisimple, there exists a dense open subset $U_0 \subseteq X_0$ such that $M_{\overline{x}}$ is semisimple for all $x \in U_0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
There exists a finite separable extension $k'/k$ such that the irreducible components of $M_{k'}$ have geometrically irreducible support. By a limit argument, we can find a dominant connected etale neighborhood $S_0' \rightarrow S_0$ inducing the extension $k'/k$ on function fields.  We can base change to $S_0'$ without changing the statement. Thus we may assume the decomposition factors of $M_k$ have geometrically irreducible support.
		
		We apply Lemma \ref{filtration_THM}. Thus we obtain a dense open subset $V_0 \subseteq S_0$ and a filtration
		\[
		0 = M_0 \subset M_1 \subset \ldots \subset M_{n - 1} \subset M_n = M.
		\] 
		by relatively perverse sheaves $M_i \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{V_0}/V_0)$. The generic geometric fiber of a graded piece $M_i/M_{i - 1}$ for $1 \leq i \leq n$ is geometrically semisimple if and only if there exists a dense subset $U_0 \subseteq S_0'$ such that the fiber over a geometric point supported in $U_0$ is geometrically simple by properties (5) and (6) of the filtration. Moreover, the connecting morphisms
		\[
		M_{i}/M_{i - 1} \rightarrow M_{i - 1}[1]
		\]
		are zero on the geometric generic fiber if and only if there exists a dense subset such that the fiber is zero over all geometric points supported at the closed points by Lemma \ref{morphismzero_LEM}. The argument for the existence of a dense open subset such that semisimplicity holds at all geometric fibers is the same.

label: critsemisimple_PROP
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{critsemisimple_PROP}
	Let $S_0$ be an integral geometrically unibranch topologically Noetherian scheme with function field $k$. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a finite type morphism. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X_0)$. Then $K_{\overline{k}}$ is semisimple if and only if there is a dense subset $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that for all points $x \in U_0$ the restriction to the geometric fiber $K_{\overline{x}}$ is semisimple. If the generic fiber $K_{\overline{k}}$ is semisimple, then there exists a dense open subset $V_0 \subseteq S_0$ such that $K_{\overline{x}}$ is semisimple for all $x \in V_0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We can apply Lemma \ref{morphismzero_LEM} to the connecting morphisms
	\[
	{}^{{\mathfrak{p}}/S_0}\mathscr{H}^{i + 1}(K)[i + 1] \rightarrow {}^{{\mathfrak{p}}/S_0} \tau^{\leq i}(K)[1]
	\]
	for $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ to prove that we have a decomposition
	\[
	K_{\overline{k}} = \bigoplus_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{i}(K_{\overline{k}})[-i]
	\]
	over the generic point if and only if there exists a dense subset $U_0\subseteq S_0$ such that 
	\[
	K_{\overline{x}} = \bigoplus_{i \in \mathbb{Z}} {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{i}(K_{\overline{x}})[-i]
	\]
	for all points $x \in U_0$. We can then apply Lemma \ref{critsemisimpleperv_LEM} to the relative perverse cohomology sheaves to obtain the statement. The argument for the existence of a dense open subset such that semisimplicity holds at all points in the dense open subset is the same.

label: decomposition1_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{decomposition1_THM}
		Let $k$ be a separably closed field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be $k$-schemes and $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ a proper morphism of $k$-schemes. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X)$ be a semisimple arithmetic complex. The pushforward $f_*(K)$ is semisimple.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that $K$ splits into a direct sum of shifted irreducible arithmetic perverse sheaves by Theorem \ref{subquotientsarithmetic_THM}. Thus we can assume $K$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf. The schemes, the morphism, and the perverse sheaf descend to an arithmetic field by a limit argument and Corollary \ref{models_COR}. Hence we can assume the schemes $X$ and $Y$, the morphism $X \rightarrow Y$, and the complex $K$ are defined over an arithmetic field $k_0$.
	
	We first consider the case when $k$ is the algebraic closure of a finite field. In this case, $k_0$ is finite and $K$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf on $X$. By Lafforgue's theorem \cite[Cor.~VII.8]{LafforguePurity}, we can twist $K$ by a character of $k$ and assume the perverse sheaf $K$ is pure of weight zero. By \cite[Stab.~5.1.14]{BBD}, the pushforward $f_*(K)$ is pure of weight zero. Thus \cite[Cor.~5.4.6]{BBD} implies that $f_*(K)$ is geometrically semisimple.  
			
	We turn to the general case. There is an irreducible regular arithmetic scheme $S_0$ with function field isomorphic to $k_0$ by Lemma \ref{modelbasic_LEM}. After possibly shrinking $S_0$, we can find a diagram with Cartesian squares
		\[
		                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
		\begin{tikzcd}
			X \arrow[d] \arrow[r, "f"] & Y \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & k_0 \arrow[d] \\
			X_0 \arrow[r, "f"]         & Y_0 \arrow[r]         & S_0         
		\end{tikzcd}
		\] 
		such that $X_0 \rightarrow Y_0$ is proper, $k_0 \rightarrow S_0$ is the inclusion of the function field of $S_0$, and $Y_0$ is an $S_0$-scheme. After shrinking $S_0$,  Theorem \ref{extensionari_THM} shows there exists a complex $K_0 \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X_0)$  such that $K_{{k}}$ is isomorphic to $K$. After shrinking $S_0$, Proposition \ref{critsemisimple_PROP} shows we may assume $K_x$ is geometrically semisimple for all points $x \in S_0$.
		
		The residue field at a closed point in $S_0$ is finite.  Note that $K_x$ is defined over a finite field, hence $K_{\overline{x}}$ is arithmetic. Therefore, the pushforward $f_*(K_x)$ is geometrically semisimple for all closed points $x \in S_0$ by the case of finite fields already treated. By proper base change, Proposition \ref{critsemisimple_PROP} implies $f_*(K)$ is geometrically semisimple because the scheme $S_0$ is Jacobson.

label: decomposition2_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{decomposition2_THM}
		Let $k$ be a field finitely generated over a separably closed field. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(X)$ be an arithmetic semisimple complex and $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ a proper morphism. The pusforward $f_*(K)$ is semisimple.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume $K$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf since $K$ is semisimple. This implies $K_{\overline{k}}$ is semisimple. After passing to a finite extension of $k$, Theorem \ref{geomsimpleperverse_THM} implies that there exist geometrically irreducible arithmetic perverse sheaves $M_1, \ldots, M_n \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{k'})$, and continuous $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representations $\rho_1, \ldots,\rho_n$ of the Galois group of $k$ such that
		\[
		K \cong (M_1\otimes\rho_1) \oplus \ldots \oplus (M_n\otimes \rho_n).
		\]
		Note that $M_i\otimes \rho_i$ is a direct factor of a semisimple perverse sheaf, hence it is semisimple. Moreover, any perverse subsheaf $M \subseteq M_i\otimes\rho_i$ is given by $M = M_i\otimes \rho'$ for 
		\[
		\rho' = \textnormal{Hom}(M_i, M).
		\]
		Thus we obtain that $\rho_i$ is semisimple. This also shows that the tensor product of a semisimple perverse sheaf with a semisimple representation of the Galois group of $k$ is semisimple. By the projection formula, we may pass to $M_i$ for some $1 \leq i \leq n$ and assume $K$ is a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf. 
		
		Let $k_0 \subset k$ be a separably closed subfield, such that $k$ is finitely generated over $k_0$ and $k_0$ admits no finite algebraic extension in $k$ (i.e. any polynomial irreducible in $k_0$ remains irreducible in $k$). This implies $\overline{k}_0\otimes_{k_0}k$ is a field. Since $\overline{k}_0/k_0$ is purely inseparable, we may base change to $\overline{k}_0k$ and assume $k_0$ is algebraically closed. Our goal now is to write $k$ as the function field of a smooth $k_0$-scheme and then spread out $K$ over this smooth $k_0$-scheme. However, note that we want the spreading of $K$ to be arithmetic, so that we may apply the decomposition theorem for arithmetic complexes to the pushforward. This is why we will first descend $K$ to a scheme over an arithmetic field, spread it out there, and then pull the spread out complex back to $k_0$. This way we ensure that the spread out complex is arithmetic.		
				
		We may write
		\[
		k_0 = \varinjlim k_i
		\]
		as a filtered colimit over all arithmetic subfields $k_i \subset k_0$. By passing to a subsystem, we may assume that there are finitely generated extensions $k_i'/k_i$ with
		\[
		k_i'\otimes_{k_i}k_0 = k
		\] 
		and $k_i' \subset k$. After twisting $K$ by a character of the Galois group of $k$, Theorem \ref{modelsIrr_THM} allows us to assume there are schemes $X_i$ and $Y_i$ over $k'_i$ such that $X_i\times_{k'_i}k = X$, $Y_i\times_{k'_i} k = Y$, a perverse sheaf $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_i)$ with $M_k = K$, and a proper morphism
		\[
		X_i \rightarrow Y_i
		\]
		reproducing the morphism $X \rightarrow Y$ after base change. Since $K$ is a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf, we see that $M$ is a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf. 
		
		Since $k_0$ is algebraically closed, the extension $k/k_0$ is separable. Thus $k'_i/k_i$ is separable. In particular, there is a smooth $k_i$-scheme $S_i$ with function field $k'_i$. After shrinking $S_i$, we may find a proper morphism of $S_i$-schemes $X_{ii} \rightarrow Y_{ii}$ with generic fiber isomorphic to $X_i \rightarrow Y_i$. After shrinking $S_i$, Theorem \ref{extensionari_THM} shows there exists a relatively perverse universally locally acyclic sheaf $M_i \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_{ii}/S_{ii})$ with generic fiber $M_{k'_i} = M$. 
		
		We put $X_0 := X_{ii}\times_{k_i} k_0$, $Y_0 := Y_{ii}\times_{k_i} k_0$, $S_0 := S_{ii}\times_{k_i} k_0$, and $M_0 := (M_i)_{k_0}$. These schemes fit into a diagram
		\[
				                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
		\begin{tikzcd}
			X \arrow[d] \arrow[r, "f"] & Y \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & k \arrow[d] \\
			X_0 \arrow[r, "f"]         & Y_0 \arrow[r]         & S_0         
		\end{tikzcd}
		\]
		with Cartesian squares. Let $d$ be the dimension of $S_0$. Since $S_0$ is smooth over $k_0$, Lemma \ref{irred_LEM} implies $M_0[d]$ is an irreducible perverse sheaf on $X_0$. Thus $M_0$ is a semisimple complex. Note that $M_0$ descends to the arithmetic field $k_i$, so $M_0$ is arithmetic. Therefore, Theorem \ref{decomposition1_THM} implies $f_*(M_0)$ is a semisimple complex. Lemma \ref{irred_LEM} and proper base change imply that $f_*(K)$, the restriction of $f_*(M_0)$ to the generic fiber over $S_0$, is semisimple.

label: hardlefschetz_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{hardlefschetz_THM}
		Let $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a projective morphism of $k$-schemes. Let $\eta \in H^2(X, \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(1))$ be the Chern class of a $f$-ample line bundle on $X$ and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X)$ a geometrically semisimple arithmetic perverse sheaf. The morphism
		\[
		\eta^i\colon {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{-i}(f_*(M)) \rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{i}(f_*(M))(i)
		\]
		is an isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We can pass to the algebraic closure of $k$ without changing the statement, thus we can assume $k$ to be algebraically closed. Because $M$ is semisimple, we can assume $M$ is irreducible by Theorem \ref{subquotientsarithmetic_THM}. 
		
		As in the proof of the decomposition theorem, we can arrive at a diagram
		\[
		                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
		\begin{tikzcd}
			X \arrow[d] \arrow[r, "f"] & Y \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & k_0 \arrow[d] \\
			X_0 \arrow[r, "f"]         & Y_0 \arrow[r]         & S_0         
		\end{tikzcd}
		\] 
		such that there exists $M_0 \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_0/S_0)$ over $S_0$ with restriction to the generic fiber isomorphic to $M$, the $f$-ample line bundle on $X$ spreads out to a $f$-ample line bundle on $X_0$. The $f$-ample line bundle gives rise to a morphism $\eta\colon \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell \rightarrow \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell(1)[2]$ in the derived category of proetale sheaves on $X_0$ such that the fiber of this morphism over each point of $S_0$ equals the Chern class of the $f$-ample line bundle. We consider the induced morphism on relative perverse cohomology sheaves
		\[
		\eta^i\colon ^{{\mathfrak{p}}/S_0}\mathscr{H}^{-i}(f_*(M_0)) \rightarrow{} ^{{\mathfrak{p}}/S_0}\mathscr{H}^i(f_*(M_0))(i).
		\]
		By Corollary \ref{isocrit_COR}, this morphism is an isomorphism on the generic fiber if and only if it is an isomorphism at a dense set of closed points. Thus we can reduce the Hard Lefschetz theorem to the case of finite fields (see \cite[Thm.~5.4.10]{BBD}) as in the proof of the decomposition theorem.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
We define the affine pro-algebraic group scheme
		\[
		I_\ell := \varprojlim \mu_{\ell^n}
		\]
		over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$. We denote by $\underline{I_\ell}$ the proetale sheaf representing $I_\ell$. 
		
		Let $X_0$ be a qcqs scheme and $R$ a sheaf of rings in the proetale topology on $X_0$. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}(X_0, R)$. We say $I_\ell$ \textit{acts} on $K$ if there is a group morphism
		\[
		\underline{I_\ell} \rightarrow \textnormal{Aut}_R(K)
		\]
		of proetale sheaves on $X_0$. We say the action by $I_\ell$ on $K$ is \textit{quasi-unipotent} if for each weakly etale neighborhood $X_0' \rightarrow X_0$, and each $t \in I_\ell(X_0')$, the action by $t$ on $K_{X_0'}$ is quasi-unipotent.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Although the sheaf $\underline{I_\ell}$ is naturally isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_\ell(1)$, we prefer to keep the notation above to indicate an inertia group.
		
		Furthermore, we remark that an action by $I_\ell$ is automatically continuous. Roughly speaking, any proetale sheaf is also a sheaf of condensed sets. The action by $I_\ell$ is always an action by a condensed sheaf of group on a condensed sheaf. Thus it is continuous.

label: qunimon_PROP
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By devissage, we may assume $K$ is a locally constant sheaf $F$ on $X_0$. By a further devissage, we may assume $X_0$ is integral (see \cite[Cor.~2.3.4]{hansen2025arithmeticpropertieselladicetale} for more details on the devissage). By \cite[Rem.~7.4.8]{BhattSPE}, lisse proetale sheaves on $X_0$ are classified by the proetale fundamental group. We can find a connected weakly etale torsor
		\[
		X_0' \rightarrow X_0
		\] 
		which trivializes the lisse sheaf $\underline{I_\ell}$ by adding all the $\ell$'th roots of unity to $X_0$ and passing to a connected component.\footnote{One could also show that $X_0'$ is topologically Noetherian. If $X_0$ is Noetherian, then $X_0'$ is Noetherian as well (see \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05KG}{Tag 05KG}]{stacks-project}).} Since $X_0'$ is a torsor over a topologically Noetherian scheme, \cite[Rem.~7.4.8]{BhattSPE} implies that lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaves on $X_0'$ are classified by the proetale fundamental group. In particular, a morphism of lisse sheaves on $X_0'$ is zero if and only if it is zero at a point. Thus we may pass to a fiber of $F$ over a point in $X_0$ and assume $X_0$ is a field. 
				
		In this case, $F$ is given by a continuous finite-dimensional Galois representation $\rho$ of $k$ such that no finite extension of $k$ admits all $\ell$'th roots of unity and we are given an morphism of proetale sheaves
		\[
		\underline{I_\ell} \rightarrow \textnormal{Aut}(\rho). 
		\]
		We add all the $\ell$'th roots of unity to $k$ and obtain an extension $k'/k$. We have an injection
		\[
		\textnormal{Gal}(k'/k) \rightarrow (\mathbb{Z}_\ell)^*
		\]
		The image is open: the group $(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)^*$ is a $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-module of rank one and finite torsion part. The image of the Galois group is infinite and closed, by compactness of the Galois group. Thus it must be a $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-submodule of $(\mathbb{Z}_\ell)^*$. Because the image is infinite, it must have rank one as a $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-module. This implies that the image is open. In particular, we note that there is $n \geq 1$ such that $t := 1 + \ell^n$ lies in the Galois group of $k'/k$. 
		
		We choose a trivialization $I_\ell|_{k'} \cong \mathbb{Z}_\ell$. This allows us to construct a morphism of groups
		\[
		\alpha\colon \mathbb{Z}_\ell \rightarrow \textnormal{Aut}(\rho|_{k'}).
		\]
		We have a commutative diagram
		\[
		                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
		\begin{tikzcd}
			\mathbb{Z}_\ell \arrow[d, "t"] \arrow[r] & \textnormal{Aut}(\rho|_{k'}) \arrow[d, "t"] \\
			\mathbb{Z}_\ell \arrow[r]                & \textnormal{Aut}(\rho|_{k'}).               
		\end{tikzcd}
		\]
		The morphism on the right is given by conjugation by $t$ and the morphism on the left is multiplication by $t$. Thus we obtain the relation
		\[
		t\alpha(1) = \alpha(t)t. 
		\]
		Let $\lambda \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^*$ be an eigenvalue of $\alpha(1)$ and $x \in \rho$ an eigenvector. Then we have
		\[
		\lambda (tx) = \alpha(t)(tx).
		\] 
		We see that $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $\alpha(t) = \alpha(1)^{1 + \ell^n}$. Thus $\lambda^{1/1 + \ell^n}$ is an eigenvalue of $\alpha(1)$. Since $\rho$ is finite-dimensional, there are $k, k'> 0$ with
		\[
		\lambda^{1/(1 + \ell^n)^k} = \lambda^{1/(1 + \ell^n)^{k + k'}}
		\] 
		Thus $\lambda$ is a root of unity. Since the action of $I_\ell$ is continuous, we see that all elements of $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$ act by roots of unity by considering eigenspaces in an isotypical decomposition of $\rho$ under $I_\ell$. 
		
		We define a morphism of proetale sheaves
		\[
		\Tilde{N}\colon \underline{I_\ell} \rightarrow \textnormal{End}_R(K, K)
		\]
		as follows: Let $X_0' \rightarrow X_0$ be a weakly etale neighborhood of $X_0$. Let $t \in \underline{I_\ell}(X_0')$. The action by $\rho(t)$ is quasi-unipotent on $K|_{X_0'}$ by (1), so we can put
		\[
		\Tilde{N}(t) := \frac{\textnormal{log}(\rho(nt))}{n}
		\]
		for a sufficiently large natural number $n \geq 1$ such that $\rho(nt)$ is unipotent. This defines a group morphism.
		
		We can now tensor the above morphism
		\[
		\underline{I_\ell}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell} \textnormal{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \rightarrow \textnormal{End}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell}(K, K)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell} \textnormal{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell). 
		\]
		Tensor product functoriality induces an isomorphism
		\[
		\textnormal{End}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell}(K, K)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell} \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \rightarrow \textnormal{End}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell}(K\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell} \underline{I_\ell}, K)
		\]
		Note that we have an isomorphism
		\[
		\underline{I_\ell} = \textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\mathbb{Z}_\ell, \underline{I_\ell}).
		\]
		Thus we obtain
		\begin{align*}
		\underline{I_\ell}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell} \textnormal{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) &= 	\textnormal{End}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\mathbb{Z}_\ell, \underline{I_\ell})\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell} \textnormal{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \\
		&= \textnormal{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \underline{I_\ell})
		\end{align*}
		We may compose and obtain the morphism
		\[
		\Tilde{\Tilde{N}}\colon \textnormal{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}(\underline{I_\ell}, \underline{I_\ell})\rightarrow \textnormal{Hom}_{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell}(K\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}\underline{I_\ell}, K).
		\]
		We define
		\[
		N := \Tilde{\Tilde{N}}(X_0)(\textnormal{id}).
		\]
		This defines the nilpotent monodromy operator
		\[
		N\colon K(1) \rightarrow K
		\]
		because $K\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}\underline{I_\ell} = K(1)$ by definition of the Tate twist.

title: Definition

Let $S_0$ be the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring and $\pi \in S_0$ a uniformizer. We define
		\[
		\Tilde{S}_0 := S_0\big[\pi^{1/\ell^n}~|~ n \geq 1\big].
		\]

		\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(K) := \tilde{i}^*\tilde{j}_*\tilde{j}^*(K_{\Tilde{V}_0}) \in \textnormal{D}(X_s, R).

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{prolncbc_LEM}Let $S$ be the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring. We assume one of the following two conditions on the coefficient ring $R$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item The ring $R$ is Noetherian and complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$. The characteristic of $R/I$ is invertible on $S$.
			\item The ring $R$ is $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ for a prime $\ell$ invertible on $S$.
		\end{enumerate}
		Let $S' \rightarrow S$ be a morphism of spectra of discrete valuation rings. We assume there is a uniformizer $\pi \in \Gamma(S, \mathcal{O}_S)$ mapping to a uniformizer $\pi' \in \Gamma(S', \mathcal{O}_{S'})$. Let $X$ be an $S$-scheme and $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X_\eta, R)$ a constructible complex on the generic fiber of $X$ over $S$. We denote by $\pi\colon X_{S'} \rightarrow X$ the projection induced by base change. We have an $I_\ell$-equivariant natural isomorphism
		\[
		\pi^*(\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(K)) = \Psi^\ell_{\pi'}(\pi^*(K)). 
		\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that we can always construct a natural morphism 
		\[
		\pi^*(\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(K)) \rightarrow \Psi^\ell_{\pi'}(\pi^*(K)).
		\]
		To prove this morphism is an isomorphism, we may pass to the strict henselization of $S$ and $S'$ by smooth base change. Thus we may assume $S$ and $S'$ are strict traits.
	
	Let $I^{(\ell)}_{S}$ and $I^{(\ell)}_{S'}$ be the kernel of the morphism $I \rightarrow I^\ell$ from the inertia group to the maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient for the inertia of $S$ and $S'$ respectively. We can now write
	\begin{align*}
	\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(K) &= \Psi(K)^{I^{(\ell)}_{S}} \\
	\Psi^\ell_{\pi'}(\pi^*(K)) &= \Psi(\pi^*(K))^{I^{(\ell)}_{S'}}.
	\end{align*}
	It follows from the change of trait isomorphism that we have an isomorphism
	\[
	\pi^*(\Psi(K))^{I^{(\ell)}_{S}} = \Psi(\pi^*(K))^{I^{(\ell)}_{S'}}
	\]
	This isomorphism identifies with the morphism constructed above. Thus we obtain the desired isomorphism.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{prolfamily_THM}
		Let $S_0$ be an irreducible qcqs scheme. We assume one of the following two conditions on the coefficient ring $R$:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item The ring $R$ is a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$. We assume the characteristic of $R/I$ is invertible on $S_0$.
			\item The ring $R$ is $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ for a prime $\ell$ invertible on $S_0$. 
		\end{enumerate}
		Let $C_0$ be a finitely presented smooth $S_0$-scheme with geometrically connected fibers of dimension one and $\pi \in \Gamma(C_0, \mathcal{O}_{C_0})$ a global section of the structure sheaf of $C_0$. We define $Y_0 :=V(\pi)$ to be the zero-locus of $\pi$. We assume $Y_0$ is an relative normal crossing divisor with connected fibers over $S_0$. Let
		\[
		f\colon X_0 \rightarrow C_0
		\]
		be a morphism of $S_0$-schemes. We consider a constructible complex $K_0 \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X_0, R)$. There exists a constructible dense open subscheme $U_0 \subseteq S_0$ and a complex $$\Psi^{\ell}_\pi(K) \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X_0, R)$$ with an action by $I_\ell$ such that such that we have a natural $I_\ell$-equivariant isomorphism
		\[
		\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(K)_x = \Psi^{\ell}_{\pi_x}(K_{x})
		\]
		for all $x \in U_0$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Remark \ref{genbcqcqs_REM}, we may assume $R$ is a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$. We denote by $U_0 \subseteq C_0$ the complement of $Y_0$. We define the scheme
		\[
		\Tilde{C}_0 := C_0[\pi^{1/\ell^n}~|~ n \geq 1].
		\]
	Note that $\Tilde{C}_0$ admits an action by $I_\ell$ over $C_0$. Let $\tilde{i}\colon Y_0 \rightarrow \Tilde{C}_0$ be the closed inclusion of the reduced preimage of $Y_0$ in $\Tilde{C}_0$ and $\tilde{j}\colon \Tilde{U}_0 \rightarrow \Tilde{C}_0$ the inclusion of the complement. We put
	\[
	\Psi_\pi^\ell(K) := \Tilde{i}^*\Tilde{j}_*\Tilde{j}^*(K_{\Tilde{C}_0}).
	\]
	This object naturally comes with an action by $I_\ell$ because $\Tilde{C}_0$ admits an action by $I_\ell$ over $C_0$. Our goal is to show that this complex is constructible and that the formation of the above functor commutes with base-change generically. Once this is achieved, the definition of the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles implies that this functor is naturally isomorphic to the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles formed over each fiber. 
	
	To prove those assertions, we may assume $S_0$ contains all $\ell$'th roots of unity by adjoining all $\ell$'th roots of unity to $S_0$ and passing to an irreducible component. The resulting integral morphism to $S_0$ is weakly etale because $\ell$ is invertible on $S_0$. By weakly etale base change, it is sufficient if we prove the claim assuming $S_0$ admits all $\ell$'th roots of unity.
	
	This allows us to choose a trivialization $I_\ell \cong \mathbb{Z}_\ell$. Then $\Tilde{C}_0$ is a $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-torsor over $U_0$. Let us denote by $q\colon \Tilde{C}_0 \rightarrow C_0$ the natural projection. Then we have
	\[
	q^{-1}(Y_0)^{\textnormal{red}} = Y_0.
	\]
	We see that $$\mathscr{L} := q_*(R)$$ is a constructible $R[[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]]$-module over the Iwasawa algebra $R[[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]]$.
	
                                                                                                                                                                                 
    
                                                                        
    
                        
    
                                                      
     
                             
	We identify the Iwasawa algebra $R[[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]] \cong R[[t]]$ with a power series ring over $R$. The ring $R[[t]]$ is a Noetherian ring, complete with respect to the ideal $(I, t) \subset R[[t]]$. Therefore, Theorem \ref{genbc_THM} and the projection formula for integral morphisms implies we may shrink $S_0$ and assume the formation of $\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)$ commutes with base change. Loc. cit. also permits us to assume $\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)$ is constructible over $R[[t]]$. Since we know the formation of $\Psi^\ell_\pi(K)$ commutes with base-change, we have
	\[
	\Psi^\ell_\pi(K\otimes_R R/I) = \Psi^\ell_\pi(K)\otimes_R R/I
	\]
	by the projection formula for pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles over a field and constructibility of the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles over the Iwasawa algebra. This permits us to reduce to the discrete Noetherian coefficient ring $\Lambda := R/I$. 
	
	There exists a finite constructible partition of $X_0$ such that the cohomology sheaves of $\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)\otimes_{\Lambda[[t]]} \Lambda[[t]]/t$ are locally constant with perfect stalks over each stratum. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                     
	 We want to prove there is $n \geq 1$ such that the natural projection
	\[
	\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)\otimes_{\Lambda[[t]]} \Lambda[[t]]/t^{n + k}\rightarrow \Psi_\pi^\ell(K)\otimes_{\Lambda[[t]]} \Lambda[[t]]/t^n
	\]
	is an isomorphism for all $k \geq 0$. To prove this isomorphism, it is sufficient if we prove it for one point on each stratum. Since the formation of the above complexes commutes with base-change, we may prove this isomorphism assuming $S_0$ is a field. In this case, it follows from the constructibility of the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles. 
	
	Since $\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)$ is $t$-derived complete, we obtain an isomorphism
	\[
	\Psi_\pi^\ell(K) = \Psi^\ell_\pi(K)\otimes_{\Lambda[[t]]} \Lambda[[t]]/t^n.
	\]
	The complex on the right is a constructible complex with coefficients in $\Lambda[[t]]/t^n$. Since this ring is a finite free module over $\Lambda$, we see that the complex $\Psi^\ell_f(K)$ has locally constant cohomology sheaves with perfect stalks over $\Lambda$ over the same partition as above. Note that we may find a finite filtration of $\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)$ with subquotients isomorphic to $\Psi_\pi^\ell(K)\otimes_{\Lambda[[t]]}\Lambda[[t]]/t$. This complex is classical, so the complex $\Psi^\ell_f(K)$ is classical by \cite[Cor.~5.2.9]{BhattSPE} and \cite[Prop.~5.2.6]{BhattSPE}.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $X$ be a $k$-scheme and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X)$ a perverse sheaf with a nilpotent operator $N\colon M(1) \rightarrow M$. Let $f \colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a morphism of $k$-schemes. We say \textit{$f$ satisfies the monodromy property with respect to $M$} if the filtration induced by the spectral sequence
		\[
		E_1^{pq} := {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\textnormal{Gr}_{-q}^M(M))) \Rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(M))
		\]
		equals the monodromy filtration on ${}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{i}(f_*(M))$ for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$. 
		
		We assume $k$ is finite. We say $M$ is \textit{monodromy pure of weight $w \in \mathbb{Z}$} if the graded pieces of the monodromy filtration $\textnormal{Gr}_i^M(M)$ are pure of weight $w + i$ for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$.

label: weightmon_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{weightmon_THM}
		Let $S$ be the strict henselization of a discrete valuation ring essentially of finite type over a field with uniformizer $\pi \in S$. Let $X$ be an $S$-scheme and $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_{{\eta}})$ a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf which admits a model over an arithmetic field (see Definition \ref{model_DEF}). Let $\rho\colon I^\ell_S \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}(\rho)$ be an indecomposable unipotent representation of the pro-$\ell$ inertia of $S$. We have:
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item The action of $I_\ell$ on $\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M\otimes \rho)$ is quasi-unipotent.
			\item The graded pieces of the monodromy filtration on $\textnormal{Gr}^M_i(\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M\otimes \rho))$ are geometrically semisimple for all $i \in \mathbb{Z}$. 
			\item Let $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a proper morphism of $S$-schemes. The monodromy spectral sequence
			\[
			E_1^{pq} := {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\textnormal{Gr}_{-q}^M(\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M\otimes\rho)))) \Rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M\otimes\rho)))
			\]
			degenerates on the second page. Moreover, the morphism $f$ satisfies the monodromy property with respect to $\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M\otimes\rho)$. 
		\end{enumerate}

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{weightmonodromyfinite_THM}
		Let $k$ be a finite field. Let $C$ be a smooth curve over $k$ and $0 \in C$ a point. Let $X$ be a $C$-scheme. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X)$ be pure of weight $w \in \mathbb{R}$. The pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles $\Psi^\ell_{0}(M)$ are monodromy pure of weight $w$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The nearby cycles $\Psi(M)$ are monodromy pure of weight $w$ by \cite[Sec.~5]{beilinsonbernsteinjantzen}. Let $I^{(\ell)}$ be the kernel of the natural projection $I \rightarrow I^\ell$ from the inertia of $S$ to the maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient of the inertia of $S$. We have an $I^\ell$-equivariant isomorphism
		\[
		\Psi^\ell_0(M) = \Psi(M)^{I^{(\ell)}}.
		\]
		by Remark \ref{prolnc_REM}. All finite quotients of $I^{(\ell)}$  are of order co-prime to $\ell$. Thus $I^{(\ell)}$ acts on $\Psi(M)$ through a finite quotient. In particular, the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles are a direct factor of the nearby cycles. This implies that the graded pieces of the monodromy filtration of $\Psi^{\ell}_0(M)$ are a direct factor of the graded pieces of the monodromy filtration of $\Psi(M)$. Thus the monodromy filtration on $\Psi^{\ell}_0(M)$ is monodromy pure of weight $w$.

label: puretensor_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{puretensor_LEM}
		Let $k$ be a finite field and $X$ a $k$-scheme. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(X)$ and $N\colon M(1) \rightarrow M$ a nilpotent operator. Let $\rho$ be a representation of the Galois group of $k$, equipped with a nilpotent operator $N\colon \rho(1) \rightarrow \rho$. We assume the monodromy filtrations on $M$ and $\rho$ are monodromy pure of weight $w, w' \in \mathbb{Z}$ respectively. The tensor product $M\otimes \rho$ is monodromy pure of weight $w + w'$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. Proposition \ref{tensorformula_PROP} shows
		\[
		\textnormal{Gr}^M_k(M\otimes V) = \bigoplus_{i + j = k} \textnormal{Gr}^M_i(M)\otimes\textnormal{Gr}^M_j(V)
		\]
		Tensoring a pure sheaf of weight $w + i$ with a pure Galois representation of weight $w' + j$ gives a pure perverse sheaf of weight $$w + w' + i + j = w + w' + k,$$ hence the claim.
