title: Proof
body_md:
We begin by constructing an auxiliary sheaf on a geometrically connected regular curve $C$ over a field $k$ with a morphism $S \rightarrow C$ such that the closed point maps to a rational point $0 \in C(k)$ and the induced map on the pro-$\ell$ inertia
	\[
	I^t_S \rightarrow I_0^t
	\] 
	is an isomorphism. We choose a morphism
	\[
	C \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^1_{k}
	\]
	which is unramified at $0$. Let $k_0 \subset k$ be the prime field, then we compose this morphism with the natural projection
	\[
	\mathbb{A}^1_k \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^1_{k_0}.
	\]
	Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $S$, then we have the composition
	\[
	\eta \rightarrow \mathbb{G}_{m, \overline{k}_0}.
	\]
	This map induces an isomorphism
	\[
	I^\ell_{S} \xrightarrow{\sim} \pi_1^{\ell}(\mathbb{G}_{m, \overline{k}_0}).
	\]
	By composing the inverse of this isomorphism with $\rho$, we obtain a lisse $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-sheaf $\Tilde{\mathscr{L}}_0$ on $\mathbb{G}_{m, \overline{k}_0}$. Since the representation $\rho$ is unipotent and indecomposed, it is isomorphic to a Jordan block of some dimension. One can check from this that the conjugation action by the Galois group of the base field $k_0$ does not change the isomorphism type of $\Tilde{\mathscr{L}}_0$. Thus we find that the sheaf $\Tilde{\mathscr{L}}_0$ descends to a sheaf over a finite extension of the prime field $k_0$. We replace $k_0$ by a finite extension so that $\Tilde{\mathscr{L}}_0$ descends to the new base field. Let $j\colon \mathbb{G}_{m, k_0} \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^1_{k_0}$ be the inclusion, then we denote by $\mathscr{L}_0$ the pullback of $j_!(\Tilde{\mathscr{L}}_{0})$ to $C$. This gives a constructible etale sheaf on $C$, lisse outside the fiber of $C \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^1_{k}$ over 0, such that the inertia representation at $0$ is isomorphic to $\rho$. Note that the sheaf $\mathscr{L}_0$ admits a model over an arithmetic field. Moreover, when the base field $k$ is finite, we see that the representation of the decomposition group at 0 is monodromy pure, at least after a twist, because it only has only one one-dimensional primitive part.
	
  
                                                                                                                                                                                             
    
                                                               
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
    
                                  
    
  
	We can write
	\[
	S = \varprojlim C_i
	\]
	as a cofiltered limit over regular geometrically connected curves over arithmetic fields (which increase with $i$). Since $X$ is finitely presented over $S$, we may write
	\[
	X = \varprojlim X_i
	\]
	as a cofiltered limit of $C_i$-schemes. The uniqueness of models noted in Remark \ref{uniquenessmodels_REM} allows us to assume $M$ descends to the generic fiber of $X_i$. The morphisms
	\[
	S \rightarrow \textnormal{Spec}(\mathcal{O}_{C_i, 0})
	\]
	induce an isomorphism on pro-$\ell$ inertia. Since the formation of pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles commutes with base-change along such morphisms by Lemma \ref{prolncbc_LEM}, we may assume $S$ is the strict henselization of a local ring of a regular geometrically connected curve $C$ over an arithmetic field $k_0$. Moreover, we may assume the perverse sheaf $M$ exists on the generic fiber of the morphism $X \rightarrow C$. After a finite extension of $k_0$, we may assume the curve $C$ is smooth and the point $0 \in C$ is rational over $k_0$. Since $k_0$ is arithmetic, we see that the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles $\Psi^\ell_0(M)$ satisfy the quasi-unipotent monodromy theorem by Proposition \ref{qunimon_PROP}. Thus we obtain (1).
	
	By Lemma \ref{modelfields_LEM}, there exists an arithmetic regular connected base-scheme $S_0$ with function field $k_0$. After shrinking $S_0$, we may assume there exists a smooth $S_0$-scheme $C_0$ with geometrically connected fibers of dimension 1, a section $S_0 \rightarrow C_0$, $S_0$-schemes $X_0$ and $Y_0$, and a proper morphism $X_0 \rightarrow Y_0$, such that these objects reproduce the corresponding previous objects over the generic fiber of $S_0$. By Theorem \ref{extensionari_THM}, we may assume the perverse sheaf $M$ extends to a relatively perverse universally locally acycic sheaf $M_0 \in \textnormal{Perv}^{\textnormal{ULA}}(X_0/S_0)$, after shrinking $S_0$. By shrinking $S_0$ further, Proposition \ref{critsemisimple_PROP} permits us to assume the fiber of $M_0$ over each point in $S_0$ is geometrically irreducible.
	
	By the generic constructibility theorem proven above, we may shrink $S_0$ and assume there exists a constructible complex
	\[
	\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M_0\otimes \mathscr{L}_0) \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X_{S_0})
	\] 
	with an action by $I_\ell$ such that $\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M_0)_{k_0}$ is $I_\ell$-equivariantly isomorphic to $\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M)$. By generic universal local acyclicity, we may shrink $S_0$ and assume $\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M_0)$ is ULA over $S_0$.
	
	Since the scheme $S_0$ is arithmetic, the quasi-unipotent monodromy theorem from Proposition \ref{qunimon_PROP} implies that there is a nilpotent monodromy operator
	\[
	N\colon \Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M_0\otimes\mathscr{L}_0)(1) \rightarrow \Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M_0\otimes\mathscr{L}_0).
	\]
	Since this is a morphism in the abelian category of relatively perverse universally locally acyclic sheaves over $S_0$, we can form the monodromy filtration over $S_0$. Note that this filtration reproduces the monodromy filtration over each point in $S_0$ because the passage to a fiber is $t$-exact by definition of the relatively perverse $t$-structure.
	
	Proposition \ref{critsemisimple_PROP} shows that the monodromy filtration has geometrically semisimple graded pieces over the generic fiber if and only if the monodromy filtration has geometrically semisimple graded pieces over a dense subset of closed points of $S_0$. Since the fiber of $M_0$ over each closed point of $S_0$ is geometrically irreducible, we may assume $S_0$ is a finite field to prove point (2).
	
	We consider the spectral sequence
	\[
	E_1^{pq} := {}^{{\mathfrak{p}}/S_0}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\textnormal{Gr}_{-q}^M(\Psi^\ell_\pi(M_0)))) \Rightarrow {}^{{\mathfrak{p}}/S_0}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\Psi^\ell_\pi(M_0)))
	\]
	The monodromy filtration and the pushforward commute with passage to a fiber. Therefore, the formation of this spectral sequence commutes with base-change.
	
	In particular, Lemma \ref{morphismzero_LEM} shows that the spectral sequence over the generic fiber degenerates on the second page if and only if the spectral sequence degenerates on the second page over a dense subset of closed points. To prove point (3), we may therefore assume $S_0$ is a finite field.
	
	Moreover, we can consider the filtration induced by the above spectral sequence on the relative perverse cohomology sheaves of $f_*(\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M_0))$. The formation of these images commutes with passage to fibers by $t$-exactness of passage to fibers. Moreover, we may utilize the existence of the nilpotent operator on $\Psi^\ell_{\pi}(M_0)$ to construct a monodromy operator on the relative perverse cohomology sheaves of the pushforward. We can then form the monodromy filtration in the relative perverse category over $S_0$. By $t$-exactness of passage to fibers, the formation of the relative monodromy filtration commutes with passage to fibers. 
	
	Thus we have two filtrations on each relatively perverse cohomology sheaf of the pushforward of the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles. By taking intersections, we can appeal to Corollary \ref{isocrit_COR} to show that the two filtrations agree on the generic fiber if and only if they agree at a dense subset of closed points. To prove point (4), we may therefore assume $S_0$ is a finite field. Thus we have reduced the proof of points (2), (3), and (4) to the case when $S_0$ is a finite field. 
	
	In fact, the reduction shows that we are in the following situation: we have a finite field $k_0$, two $k_0$-schemes $X_0$ and $Y_0$, a smooth geometrically connected curve $C_0$, a point $0 \in C_0$, and morphisms
	\[
	X_0 \xrightarrow{f} Y_0 \rightarrow C_0.
	\]
	Furthermore, we have a geometrically irreducible perverse sheaf $M_0 \in \textnormal{Perv}(X_0)$. After twisting $M_0$, we may assume $M_0$ is pure of weight zero by \cite[Cor.~VII.8]{LafforguePurity}. Morever, we also have the sheaf $\mathscr{L}_0$ on $C_0$. Since the monodromy filtration of $\mathscr{L}_0$ at $0$ only has one primitive part, we may twist $\mathscr{L}_0$ and assume it is monodromy pure of weight zero.
	
	Then, the projection formula shows that we have an inertia equivariant isomorphism
	\[
	\Psi^{\ell}_0(M_0\otimes\mathscr{L}_0) \cong \Psi^{\ell}_0(M_0)\otimes \Psi^{\ell}_0(\mathscr{L}_0)
	\] 
	Note that $\Psi^{\ell}_0(\mathscr{L}_0)$ is monodromy pure of weight zero, because the representation of the decomposition group of $C_0$ at $0$ induced by $\mathscr{L}_0$ is monodromy pure of weight zero. Therefore, Theorem \ref{weightmonodromyfinite_THM} and Lemma \ref{puretensor_LEM} show that $$\textnormal{Gr}^M_n(\Psi^{\ell}_0(M_0\otimes \mathscr{L}_0))$$ is pure of weight $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Thus we see that the graded pieces are geometrically semisimple, i.e. we obtain (2).
	
	We consider the monodromy spectral sequence
	\[
	E_1^{pq} := {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\textnormal{Gr}_{-q}^M(\Psi^\ell_0(M\otimes\rho)))) \Rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{p + q}(f_*(\Psi^\ell_0(M\otimes\rho))).
	\]
	Note that the monodromy filtration on the pushforward is monodromy pure of weight zero by \cite[Stab.~5.1.14]{BBD}, Lemma \ref{puretensor_LEM}, and the projection formula. Therefore, the maps of this spectral sequence must vanish on the second page, i.e. the spectral sequence degenerates on the second page. To prove the monodromy property, we can now apply \cite[Prop.~7.7]{esnault2025semistablelefschetzpencils}.

title: Proof
body_md:
We first note that it is sufficient to prove the statements for the quasi-unipotent nearby cycles $\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}(M)$, by which we mean the direct factor of $\Psi^t(M)$ on which inertia acts quasi-unipotently. Indeed, the perverse sheaf $\Psi^{\textnormal{uni}}(M)$ is a direct factor of $\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}(M)$.
		
	We begin by proving that it is sufficient to provide the statement after passing to the normalization in a separable Galois extension $S' \rightarrow S$. Let $G$ be the Galois group of the extension. Let $P$ be the wild inertia subgroup of $G$. Note that $M$ pulled back to $S'$ has an action by $G$. This induces a (strict) $P$-action on the tame nearby cycles $\Psi^t_{S'}(M)$. We have
	\[
	\Psi^t_{S}(M) = \Psi^t_{S'}(M)^P.
	\]
	The action of $P$ commutes with the action of inertia on $\Psi^t_{S'}(M)$ by functoriality of the nearby cycles. Thus we obtain
	\[
	\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}_S(M) =  \Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}_{S'}(M)^P.
	\]
	Thus it is sufficient to prove the statement after restricting along $S' \rightarrow S$ because $\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}_{S'}(M)^P$ is a direct factor of $\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}_{S'}(M)$.
			
	After passing to a finite separable Galois extension of the function field of $S$, Theorem \ref{geomsimpleperverse_THM} and Theorem \ref{modelsIrr_THM} show that we may assume the perverse sheaf $M$ to be of the form $$M = M'\otimes\rho\otimes \chi$$ for a geometrically irreducible arithmetic perverse sheaf $M'$ admitting a model over an arithmetic field, an indecomposable unipotent representation $\rho\colon I^\ell \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}(\rho)$ of the pro-$\ell$ inertia of $S$, and a continuous character $\chi\colon I^\ell \rightarrow \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell^*$. Moreover, we can assume the action of inertia on $\Psi(M)$ is pro-$\ell$ because the sheaves have coefficients in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. In particular, it is sufficient if we prove the statement for the pro-$\ell$ nearby cycles for some uniformizer $\pi \in \Gamma(S, \mathcal{O}_S)$. 
	
	We remark that action of inertia on the nearby cycles $\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M')$ is quasi-unipotent by Theorem \ref{weightmon_THM}. Since we have the isomorphism
	\[
	\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M) = \Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M')\otimes \rho \otimes\chi
	\]
	by the projection formula, we see that $\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M)$ has quasi-unipotent inertia if and only if $\chi$ has finite order. 
	
	If $\chi$ does not have finite order, we obtain
	\[
	\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}(M) = 0.
	\]
	Thus we may assume $\chi$ has finite order. In this case, we obtain
	\[
	\Psi^{\textnormal{quni}}(M) = \Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M).
	\]
	Since $\chi$ has finite order, $\chi$ admits a model over an arithmetic field. Thus the perverse sheaf $M'\otimes\chi$ admits a model ver an arithmetic field. Note that we can write
	\[
	\Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}(M) = \Psi^{\ell}_{\pi}((M'\otimes\chi)\otimes\rho). 
	\]
	Thus the statement follows from Theorem \ref{weightmon_THM}.

label: topnot_PROP
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{topnot_PROP}
	Let $S_0$ be a topologically Noetherian scheme. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a morphism of finite type. Then $X_0$ is topologically Noetherian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We may assume $X_0$ and $S_0$ are affine, because the problem is Zariski local on $X_0$ (since $X_0$ is quasi-compact). By embedding $X_0$ in affine space, we may assume $X_0 = \mathbb{A}^n_{S_0}$. By induction on $n$, we may assume $X_0 = \mathbb{A}^1_{S_0}$. By Noetherian induction on $S_0$, we may assume $\mathbb{A}^{1}_{Z_0}$ is topologically Noetherian for any closed subscheme supported on a proper closed subset $Z_0 \subset S_0$. Thus we may assume $S_0$ irreducible. By passing to a dense open subscheme of $S_0$, we may assume $S_0$ is affine. By passing to the reduction of $S_0$, we may assume $S_0 = \textnormal{Spec}(R)$ is the spectrum of a topologically Noetherian domain $R$.
	
	Let 
	\[
	Z_0 \supseteq \ldots \supseteq Z_n \supseteq \ldots
	\]
	be a descending chain of closed subsets $Z_n \subseteq \mathbb{A}^1_{S_0}$ indexed by $n \in \mathbb{N}$. We want to show the chain stabilizes. Thus we may assume $Z_0 \neq \mathbb{A}^1_{S_0}$. Then there is a non-zero polynomial $f \in R[x]$ with $Z_0 \subseteq V(f)$. We write the polynomial as
	\[
	f  = a_nx^n + \ldots + a_0
	\]
	with coefficients $a_i \in R$ and $a_n \neq 0$ for $n \geq 0$. Noetherian induction implies $\mathbb{A}^{1}_{V(a_n)}$ is topologically Noetherian, thus the above chain stabilizes when intersected with $\mathbb{A}^1_{V(a_n)}$. Thus we may pass to the complement $\mathbb{A}^1_{D(a_n)}$ and assume $f$ is monic. 
	
	Suppose $n = 0$. In this case, we have $f = 1$ and hence $V(f) = \emptyset$. Thus $Z_n = \emptyset$ for all $n \geq 0$ which shows that the chain has stabilized. 
	
	Suppose $n > 0$. We consider the finite finitely presented flat morphism
	\[
	V(f) \rightarrow S_0.
	\]
	Either the generic point of $S_0$ has characteristic zero (and we set $F := \textnormal{id}_{S_0}$) or we can find an iterate of Frobenius $F\colon S_0 \rightarrow S_0$ such that
	\[
	(V(f)\times_{S_0, F} S_0)^{\textnormal{red}} \rightarrow S_0
	\]
	is generically etale. The natural projection
	\[
	(V(f)\times_{S_0, F} S_0)^{\textnormal{red}} \rightarrow V(f)
	\]
	is a universal homeomorphism. Thus it is sufficient if we show that the preimages of the closed subsets $Z_i$ in $(V(f)\times_{S_0, F} S_0)^{\textnormal{red}}$ stabilize. By the Noetherian induction hypothesis, we may restrict $S_0$ to a dense open subscheme. Thus we may assume the above morphism is finite etale. The reference \cite[Lem.~6.6.10~(3)]{BhattSPE} shows that $(V(f)\times_{S_0, F} S_0)^{\textnormal{red}}$ is topologically Noetherian. This implies that the chain of closed subsets $Z_n$ stabilizes, thus $\mathbb{A}^{1}_{S_0}$ is topologically Noetherian.

label: fundgroupsurjects_LEM
title: Lemma

\label{fundgroupsurjects_LEM}
	Let $S_0$ be an irreducible geometrically unibranch scheme with function field $k$ and $X_0$ a smooth $S_0$-scheme. If $X_0$ is connected, the generic fiber $X_k$ is connected. In particular, if $X_0$ is connected, then the morphism
		\[
		\pi_1(X_k) \rightarrow \pi_1(X_0)
		\]
	on etale fundamental groups is surjective.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: We may assume $S_0$ is normal by passing to the normalization (because the normalization of $S_0$ induces a universal homoeomorphism). Then the scheme $X_0$ is normal, hence it is irreducible. Thus the generic fiber $X_k$ is irreducible. In particular, the generic fiber is connected. This applies to all connected finite etale neighborhoods of $X_0$, thus the morphism on etale fundamental groups is surjective.

label: conjugate_DEF
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{conjugate_DEF}
		Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be modules over a commutative ring $R$. Let $H_1 \subseteq \textnormal{GL}(M_1)$ and $H_2 \subseteq \textnormal{GL}(M_2)$ be subgroups. We say $H_2$ is \textit{conjugate to a subgroup of $H_1$} if there is an isomorphism $M_1 \xrightarrow{\sim} M_2$ of $R$-modules such that the image of $H_2$ along the induced map $\textnormal{GL}(M_2) \rightarrow\textnormal{GL}(M_1)$ is contained in $H_1$. We say $H_1$ is \textit{conjugate to $H_2$} if there exists an isomorphism as above such that the image of $H_2$ along the induced isomorphism is equal to $H_1$.

label: specializationmonodromy_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{specializationmonodromy_THM}
		Let $S_0$ be a topologically Noetherian scheme. Let $X_0 \rightarrow S_0$ be a smooth morphism with geometrically connected fibers. Let $F$ be a lisse $\mathcal{O}$-sheaf on $X_0$. Let $x \in S_0$ be a point. We define the group (well-defined up to conjugacy)
		\[
		\Gamma(x) := \textnormal{im}(\pi_1(X_{\overline{x}}) \rightarrow \textnormal{GL}(F)),
		\]	 
		where $\overline{x} \rightarrow S_0$ is any geometric point supported at $x$.
		\begin{enumerate}[]\item Let $x_0, x_1 \in S_0$ be points such that $x_0 \rightsquigarrow x_1$. Then $\Gamma(x_1)$ is conjugate to a subgroup of $\Gamma(x_0)$.
		\item There exists a finite constructible partition
		\[
		S_0 = \bigsqcup_{i = 1}^n S_i
		\]
		such that for all $1 \leq i \leq n$ and for all $x, y \in S_i$, the group $\Gamma(x)$ is conjugate to $\Gamma(y)$.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Because $S_0$ is topologically Noetherian, we can find an aic valuation ring of finite rank $V_0$ and a morphism $V_0 \rightarrow S_0$ mapping the generic point of $V_0$ to $x_0$ and the special point to $x_1$. The etale fundamental group of the scheme $X_{V_0}$ classifies lisse etale sheaves by Remark \ref{etalegroupclassifies_REM}. Thus we obtain the diagram
		\[
		                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
		\begin{tikzcd}
			& \pi_1^{\textnormal{}}(X_{\overline{x}_1}) \arrow[d] &              \\
			\pi_1^{\textnormal{}}(X_{\overline{x}_0}) \arrow[r, two heads] & \pi_1^{\textnormal{}}(X_{V_0}) \arrow[r]             & \textnormal{GL}(F)
		\end{tikzcd}.
		\] 
		The arrow $\pi_1(X_{\eta}) \rightarrow \pi_1^{}(X_{V_0})$ is surjective by Lemma \ref{fundgroupsurjects_LEM}. Thus $\Gamma(x_0)$ is conjugate to $\Gamma(x_1)$. To prove (2), we can argue as in \cite[Thm.~8.18.2]{KatzESDE}.

label: continuousgroupmorphism_REM
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{continuousgroupmorphism_REM}
		The ring $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ admits a unique valuation extending the $\ell$-adic valuation of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$. We equip $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ with the valuation topology. For any scheme $X$ locally of finite type over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, this allows us to functorially topologize $X(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)$ by locally embedding it into affine space. 
		
		Let $G$ be a profinite group and $\mathbf{G}$ a locally algebraic group over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. A \textit{continuous group homomorphism $G \rightarrow \mathbf{G}$} means a continuous group homomorphism
		\[
		G \rightarrow \mathbf{G}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell),
		\]
		where $\mathbf{G}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)$ is equipped with the topology described above.

label: liftinglemma_LEM
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first treat the case where $\mathbf{H}$ is finite. There exists an open subgroup $U \subseteq \mathbf{G}$ such that $U\cap\mathbf{H} = \{1\}$. If we restrict the morphism $G \rightarrow \mathbf{G}/\mathbf{H}$ to the open subgroup $U$, we obtain the desired lifting because the morphism $U \rightarrow \mathbf{G}/\mathbf{H}$ is an open injection. This lifting is automatically a group morphism if $G \rightarrow \mathbf{G}/\mathbf{H}$ is a group morphism 
		
		We consider the general case. By the first step, we can lift the morphism to $\mathbf{G}/\mathbf{H}^0$. To obtain the lifting to $\mathbf{G}$, note that \cite[Prop.~5.3,~Step~1]{conradgrpcohomology} says that there is an algebraic subgroup $\mathbf{G'}  \subseteq\mathbf{G}$ such that $\mathbf{G'}\rightarrow \mathbf{G}/\mathbf{H}^0$ is an isogeny. We can lift the morphism to $\mathbf{G'}$ by the first step. By composition, we obtain a lifting of the morphism to $\mathbf{G}$.

label: prellift_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{prellift_LEM}
		Let $\rho\colon N \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}_n$ be a continuous irreducible $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-representation of a profinite group $N$. Let $G = N\ltimes H$ be the continuous product with a profinite group $H$. Suppose we have $\rho^g\cong \rho$ for all $g \in N$. There exists an open subgroup $U \subseteq H$ and a continuous lifting $\Tilde{\rho} \colon N\ltimes U \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}_n$ of $\rho$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The isomorphisms 
		\[
		\rho^g \cong \rho
		\]
	are unique up to a scalar by Schur's Lemma. Thus we obtain a continuous morphism (see \cite[Prop.~B.2]{esnault2026nonabelianversiondelignesfixed})
		\[
		H \rightarrow \mathbf{PGL}_n.
		\]
		By Lemma \ref{liftinglemma_LEM}, we can find an open subgroup $U \subseteq H$ such that there is a lifting
		\[
		\phi\colon U \rightarrow\mathbf{SL}_n.
		\]
		We can take $\Tilde{\rho}(g, x) := \rho(g)\sigma(x)$ to obtain the lifting.

label: conjactioninner_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{conjactioninner_LEM}
		Let $\mathbf{G}$ be an algebraic group over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. We assume there is a normal algebraic subgroup $\mathbf{N} \subseteq \mathbf{G}$ such that $\mathbf{N}^0$ is reductive. We consider a profinite group $G$ with a continuous morphism $\varphi\colon G \rightarrow \mathbf{G}$. There exists an open subgroup $U \subseteq G$ such that the conjugation action of $U$ on $\mathbf{N}$ is inner and induced by a continuous group homomorphism $U \rightarrow \mathbf{N}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The automorphism group of $\mathbf{N}^0$ is representable by a locally algebraic group $\underline{\textnormal{Aut}}(\mathbf{N}^0)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ (see SGA) because $\mathbf{N}^0$ is reductive. The conjugation action of $\mathbf{G}$ on $\mathbf{N}^0$ induces a morphism of group schemes
		\[
		\mathbf{G}\rightarrow \underline{\textnormal{Aut}}(\mathbf{N}^0).
		\]
		By passing to an open subgroup of $G$, we may assume the composite from $G$ to the automorphism group $\underline{\textnormal{Aut}}(\mathbf{N}^0)$ factors through the connected component of the automorphism group. The connected component is the image of the morphism induced by the conjugation action (SGA)
		\[
		\mathbf{N}^0 \rightarrow \underline{\textnormal{Aut}}(\mathbf{N}^0).
		\]
		The connected component of the kernel of this morphism is a torus, because $\mathbf{N}^0$ is reductive by assumption. By Lemma \ref{liftinglemma_LEM}, we may pass to an open subgroup of $G$ and assume the conjugation action of $G$ on $\mathbf{N}^0$ is induced by the conjugation action along a continuous group homomorphism
		\[
		\sigma\colon G \rightarrow \mathbf{N}^0.
		\]
		
		The conjugation action of $G$ on $\mathbf{N}$ factors to give an action on the finite quotient $\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0$. Since this quotient is finite, we may pass to an open subgroup of $G$ and assume the conjugation action of $G$ on $\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0$ is trivial. 
                                                                                     
     
                                          
     
                                                                                                                                                                                       
   
		
		

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
     
                                                        
     
                                                                                                                                                                                                       
     
                                                                       
     
		
		
		We compare the conjugation action induced by $\varphi$ and $\sigma$ on $\mathbf{N}$. For each $g \in G$ and $x \in \mathbf{N}$, we define
		\[
		\beta_g(x) := x\sigma(g^{-1})\varphi(g)x^{-1}\varphi(g^{-1})\sigma(g).
		\]
		Let $\mathbf{Z}$ be the center of $\mathbf{N}^0$. One can verify that
		\[
		\beta_g(x) \in \mathbf{Z}
		\]
		for all $g \in G$ and $x \in \mathbf{N}$. Moreover, we have
		\[
		\beta_g(xy) = \beta_g(x)
		\] 
		for all $y \in \mathbf{N}^0$. The group $\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0$ acts on $\mathbf{Z}$ by conjugation. With this action, the above morphism defines a crossed homomorphism. Thus we obtain a class in group cohomology 
		\[
		[\beta_g] \in H^1(\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0, \mathbf{Z}).
		\]
		The description of $H^1(\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0, \mathbf{Z})$ as crossed homomorphisms modulo principal crossed homomorphisms allows us to equip the group cohomology with the structure of an algebraic group. This implies that the cohomology group $H^1(\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0, \mathbf{Z})$ is finite by Shapiro's Lemma. Morever, the morphism 
		\[
		G \rightarrow H^1(\mathbf{N}/\mathbf{N}^0, \mathbf{Z})
		\]
		induced by $\beta$ is continuous. Thus we may pass to an open subgroup of $G$ and assume $\beta_g$ is a principal crossed homomorphism for all $g \in G$. After passing to an open subgroup of $G$, Lemma  \ref{liftinglemma_LEM} shows that the function $g \mapsto \beta_g$ can be lifted to a continuous function
		\[
		G \rightarrow \mathbf{Z},~ g \mapsto z_g
		\]
		such that
		\[
		\beta_g(x) = xz_gx^{-1}z_g^{-1}
		\]
		for all $x \in \mathbf{N}$ and $g \in G$. This relation may also be written as
		\[
		\varphi(g)^{-1}x\varphi(g) = \sigma(g)^{-1}z_gxz_g^{-1}\sigma(g)
		\]
		for all $x \in \mathbf{N}$ and $g \in G$. 
		
		Thus we obtain a continuous function
		\[
		\phi\colon G \rightarrow \mathbf{N},~g \mapsto z_g^{-1}\sigma(g). 
		\]
		such that the conjugation on $\mathbf{N}$ induced by $\phi(g)$ agrees with the conjugation induced by $\varphi(g)$ for all $g \in G$. Let $\mathbf{Z}' \subseteq \mathbf{N}$ be the center of $\mathbf{N}$. The composite
		\[
		G \xrightarrow{\phi} \mathbf{N} \rightarrow \mathbf{N}/\mathbf{Z}'
		\]
		is a continuous group morphism. By applying Lemma \ref{liftinglemma_LEM} again, we conclude that there exists a continuous group homomorphism $G \rightarrow \mathbf{N}$ inducing the conjugation action induced by $\varphi$.

label: descentmonodromy_PROP
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{descentmonodromy_PROP}
		Let $N$ be a profinite group and $\rho\colon N \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}_n$ a continuous, irreducible representation of $N$ over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. We consider a continuous semidirect product $G = H\ltimes N$ with a profinite group $H$. We denote the Zariski closure of $\rho(N)$ in $\mathbf{GL}_n$ by $\mathbf{N}$. Suppose $\rho^g\cong\rho$ for all $g \in H$. There exists an open subgroup $U \subseteq H$ and a continuous lifting $\Tilde{\rho} \colon N\ltimes U \rightarrow\mathbf{N}$ of $\rho$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By Lemma \ref{prellift_LEM}, we can assume $\rho$ lifts to a continuous group morphism $\rho'\colon N\ltimes U \rightarrow \mathbf{GL}_n$  for an open subgroup $U \subseteq H$. Let $\mathbf{G}$ be the Zariski closure of $\rho'(N\ltimes U)$ in $\mathbf{GL}_n$. By Lemma \ref{conjactioninner_LEM}, we can find a morphism $\phi\colon U \rightarrow \mathbf{N}$ such that the conjugation action of $U$ on $\mathbf{N}$ is given by $\phi$. Thus we can obtain the desired extension of the above group morphism by putting $\Tilde{\rho}(g, x) := \rho(g)\phi(x)$.

label: fibfuncperv_THM
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $n \geq 0$ and $k$ a field. An \textit{affine hyperplane} is a closed subscheme $H \subseteq \mathbb{A}^n_k$ defined by an equation of the form
	\[
	a_1x_1 + \ldots + a_nx_n = b
	\]
	for $a_i, b \in k$. For all $m \geq 0$, we define an \textit{affine $m$-hyperplane} $(H_1, \ldots, H_m)$ to be an ordered tuple of $m$ affine hyperplanes. We often identify an affine $m$-hyperplane $H$ with its union $H_1\cup \ldots\cup H_m$.
head: environment

label: hypplane_REM
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{hypplane_REM}
	Let $n \geq 0$ and $m \geq 1$. We have a parameter space of affine $m$-hyperplanes given by $X_m := \mathbb{A}^{nm + m}$. Over the parameter space, we have a universal affine $m$-hyperplane $H_m\subseteq \mathbb{A}^{n}\times X_m$ given by the union of the $m$ affine hyperplanes over each point in $X_m$. The scheme $H_m$ admits the irreducible decomposition
	\[
	H_m = H_{m, 1}\cup \ldots\cup H_{m, m}
	\] 
	because affine $m$-hyperplanes are ordered. 	We write 
	\begin{align*}
	H_1 &:= H_{m, m} \\H_2 &:= H_{m, 1}\cup \ldots \cup H_{m, m - 1}.
	\end{align*}
	
	We define the inclusions
	\begin{align*}
	i_{1}&\colon H_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n\times X_m \\
	i_2&\colon H_2 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n\times X_m \\
	i&\colon H_m \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n\times X_m.
	\end{align*}
	with corresponding complements $j_i\colon U_i \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n\times X_m$ and $j\colon U \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n\times X$ for $i = 1,2$. 
	
	We will also denote base changes of the above morphisms using the same letters. For example, we denote the inclusion
	\[
	j_2\colon U \rightarrow U_1
	\]
	by $j_2$ because it is the base-change of $j_2$ along $j_1$. 
	
	Towards the end, we would like to pass to the generic hyperplane. We write $k_m$ for the function field of $X_m$. We construct the restriction to the generic hyperplane: We have morphisms
	\[
	H_{k_m} \rightarrow H_m \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n.
	\]
	We denote pullback along this morphism by $K \mapsto K_{k_{m}}$.
head: environment

label: hypplanebasiclemma_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{hypplanebasiclemma_LEM}
	Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $n \geq 0$. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(\mathbb{A}^n_k)$. Let $i\colon H \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n_k$ be a generic affine hyperplane. The natural map
	\[
	i^*(K)(-1)[-2] \rightarrow i^!(K)
	\]
	is an isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The morphism
	\[
	\pi\colon H_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n
	\]
	is smooth. Let $i'\colon H \rightarrow H_1$ be the inclusion of a hyperplane and $i\colon H \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ the inclusion into $\mathbb{A}^n$. We are considering the canonical map
	\[
	i^*(K)\otimes i^!(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell) \rightarrow i^!(K).
	\]
	We can write $i = i'\pi$ which means that the terms are given by
	\[
	(i'\pi)^*(K)\otimes (i'\pi)^!(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell) \rightarrow (i'\pi)^!(K)
	\]
	Now note that we can also take the composite
	\begin{align*}
	(i'\pi)^*(K)\otimes (i'\pi)^!(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell) &= i'^*(\pi^*(K))\otimes (i')^!(\pi^!(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)) \\&\rightarrow (i')^!(\pi^*(K)\otimes\pi^!(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)) \\&\xrightarrow{\sim} (i')^!(\pi^!(K))
	\\& = (i'\pi)^!(K)
	\end{align*}
	Note that the second arrow is an isomorphism because $\pi$ is smooth. Moreover, this composite is equal to the composite above. Thus it is sufficient if we show that
	\[
	i'^*(\pi^*(K))\otimes (i')^!(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell) \rightarrow (i')^!(\pi^*(K))
	\]
	is an isomorphism.
	
	Note that we can write $H$ as a fiber of the morphism
	\[
	H_1 \rightarrow X_1.
	\]
	By \cite[Prop.~2.3]{Lu2022}, the canonical map for $i'$ is an isomorphism for $H \subset \mathbb{A}^n$ if $\pi^*(K)$ is universally locally acyclic over $X_1$ at each point in the fiber of $H_1 \rightarrow X_1$ over $H$. By Theorem \ref{genbc_THM}, we see that a generic hyperplane satisfies the isomorphism from the lemma.

label: hypplanesurj_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{hypplanesurj_LEM}
	Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $n \geq 0$, and $m \geq 0$. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(\mathbb{A}^n)$. Let $j\colon \mathbb{A}^n - H \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ be the complement of a generic affine $m$-hyperplane. The morphism
	\[
	j_!(M) \rightarrow M
	\]
	is a surjection of perverse sheaves.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $m = 0$, then $j$ is the identity. Thus we may assume $m > 0$.
	
	Suppose $m = 1$. The morphism is a surjection whenever ${}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{0}(i^*(M)) = 0$. Lemma \ref{hypplanebasiclemma_LEM} shows we may assume
	\[
	i^*(M)(-1)[-2] = i^!(M).
	\] 
	Thus we obtain
	\begin{align*}
		{}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{0}(i^*(M)) = {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{2}(i^!(M)) = 0
	\end{align*}
	where the last vanishing follows from the perversity of $M$ and Artin's vanishing theorem. Thus we see that the above morphism is surjective.
	
	Suppose $m > 1$. Let $j\colon \mathbb{A}^n - H_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ be the open immersion associated to the complement of a generic affine hyperplane. Let $j_2\colon \mathbb{A}^n - H_2 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ be an the complement of a generic affine  $(m - 1)$-hyperplane. The complement of the union $H_1\cup H_2$ is given by
	\[
	j = j_1j_2 = j_2j_1.
	\]
	The above morphism can be given as a composite
	\[
	j_{1!}(j_{2!}(M)) = j_{2!}(j_{1!}(M)) \rightarrow j_{1!}(M) \rightarrow M.
	\]	
	We can show the first morphism is surjective by applying the hyperplane case and the second morphism by the induction hypothesis.

label: hypplanecommute_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{hypplanecommute_LEM}
	Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $n \geq 0$. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_{c}(\mathbb{A}^n)$ and $j_1\colon U_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ an open immersion. Let $i_2\colon H_2 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ be the inclusion of a generic affine hyperplane. We put $U_2 := \mathbb{A}^n - H_2$. 
                                                                                
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                
                                                           
                                                          
              
    
	Then we have 
	\[
	j_{1!}j_{2*}(K) = j_{2*}j_{1!}(K)
	\]
	via the natural base change map.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that we have
	\begin{align*}
		i^!(K) &= i^*(K)(-1)[-2] \\
		i^!j_!(K) & =i^*j_!(K)(-1)[-2].
	\end{align*}
	because the hyperplane $H$ is generic. We have the exact triangle
	\[
	i^!(K) \rightarrow K \rightarrow k_{*}(K) \xrightarrow{+}.
	\]
	We apply $j_!$ to obtain the triangle
	\[
	j_!i^!(K) \rightarrow j_!(K) \rightarrow j_!k_*(K) \xrightarrow{+}.
	\]
	Now we have
	\[
	j_!i^!(K) = j_!i^*(K)(-1)[-2] = i^*j_!(K)(-1)[-2] = i^!j_!(K).
	\]
	We can plug this into the triangle above and obtain
	\[
	i^!j_!(K) \rightarrow j_!(K) \rightarrow j_!k_*(K)\xrightarrow{+}
	\]
	Thus we obtain an isomorphism
	\[
	j_!k_*(K) = k_*j_!(K) 
	\]	
	from the five lemma.

label: hypplanenonvanish_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{hypplanenonvanish_LEM}
	Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $n \geq 0$. Let $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(\mathbb{A}^n)$ be non-zero. For a generic $m$-hyperplane $H \subset \mathbb{A}^n$, where $m \geq n$, we have 
	\[
	H^0(\mathbb{A}^n - H, M) \neq 0.
	\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that once we have established the case $m = n$, the other cases follow trivially by considering the pushforward to the complement of a $n$-hyperplane.
	
	We argue by induction on $n$. If $n = 0$, the statement is trivial. Let $i_1\colon H_1 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ be a generic hyperplane and $i_2\colon H_2 \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ a generic $n$ hyperplane. We denote by $j_1$ and $j_2$ the inclusions of the complement into $\mathbb{A}^n$. We denote by $j$ and $i$ the open immersion/closed immersion associated to the union of $H_1\cup H_2$. We distinguish two cases.
	
	Suppose $i_1^*(M) = 0$. Then $M$ is punctual. In this case, the statement is true whenever the $n$-hyperplane avoids one point in the support of $M$. This is true for all hyperplanes outside a proper closed $X_m$, since not containing a point is a condition which gives a dense open subset of $X_m$.
	
	Thus we may assume $i_1^*(M) \neq 0$. We have
	\[
	i_1^*(M)(-1)[-2] = i_1^!(M).
	\]
	Artin's vanishing theorem implies $i_1^*(M)[-1]$ is perverse. We have an exact sequence of perverse sheaves
	\[
	0 \rightarrow M \rightarrow j_{1*}(M) \rightarrow {}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{-1}(i_1^*(M)) \rightarrow 0.
	\]
	The functor $j_{2*}$ is $t$-exact by Artin's vanishing theorem, so we obtain a short exact sequence of perverse sheaves
	\[
	0 \rightarrow j_{2*}(M) \rightarrow j_*(M) \rightarrow {j_2}_*\big({}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{-1}(i_1^*(M))\big) \rightarrow 0.
	\]
	Artin's vanishing theorem implies that we obtain a surjection
	\[
	H^0(U, M) \rightarrow H^0\big(H_1, j_{2*}\big({}^\mathfrak{p}\mathscr{H}^{-1}(i_1^*(M))\big)\big)
	\]
	We know the term on the right is non-zero for a generic hyperplane $H_2$ by induction on dimension, hence the claim.
head: environment

label: hypplanecollect_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{hypplanecollect_LEM}
	Let $k$ be a field, $n \geq 0$, and consider $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(\mathbb{A}^n)$. Let $m \geq 1$. Let $H_1$ be a generic affine hyperplane and $H_2$ a generic affine $(m - 1)$-hyperplane. 
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
     
                                                                                                                                                                                
     
		We have
		\[
		j_{1*}j_{2!}(M) = j_{2!}j_{1*}(M) .
		\]
		\item If $m \geq n$ and $M$ is non-zero, then we have
		\[
		H^0(U_2, M) \neq 0.
		\]
		\item The morphism
		\[
		{j_{1!}}(M) \rightarrow M
		\]
		is a surjection of perverse sheaves. 
	\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The first point follows from Lemma \ref{hypplanecommute_LEM}, the second point follows from Lemma \ref{hypplanenonvanish_LEM}, and the third point is given by Lemma \ref{hypplanesurj_LEM}.

label: hypplanefunctor_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{hypplanefunctor_THM}
	Let $k$ be a field and $n \geq 1$. For each $m > n$, there exists an exact, $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-linear, and faithful functor
	\[
	\alpha_m\colon \textnormal{Perv}(\mathbb{A}^n_k) \rightarrow \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell-\textnormal{fdVec}.
	\]
	The functor is given by
	\[
	\alpha_m(M) := H^0(U_2, {j_1}_!(M_{k_{m}})).
	\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $M \in \textnormal{Perv}(\mathbb{A}^n)$ is non-zero. The morphism
	\[
	{j_1}_!(M_{k_{m}}) \rightarrow M_{k_m}
	\]
	is surjective by point (3) in Lemma \ref{hypplanecollect_LEM}. Therefore, Artin vanishing implies that we have a surjection
	\[
	H^0(U_2, {j_1}_!(M_{k_m})) \rightarrow H^0(U_2, M_{k_m}).
	\]
	The term on the right does not vanish by point (2) of Lemma \ref{hypplanecollect_LEM}, so we obtain $\alpha_m(M) \neq 0$. Therefore, the above functor is faithful. Note that we have
	\[
                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  
	H^*(U_2, j_{1!}(M))= H^*(\mathbb{A}^n, j_{2*}j_{1!}(M)) = H^*(\mathbb{A}^n, j_{1!}j_{2*}(M)) = H^*_c(U_1, j_{2*}(M))
	\]
	by point (1) in Lemma \ref{hypplanecollect_LEM}. Artin's vanishing theorem implies that both sides have to be concentrated in degree zero. Therefore, the functor $\alpha_m$ is exact.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We can find a cover $X = U_1\cup \ldots \cup U_n$ by affine opens with inclusions $j_i\colon U_i\rightarrow X$. Given functors $\alpha_i\colon \textnormal{Perv}(U_i) \rightarrow \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell-\textnormal{fdVec}$ for $1 \leq i \leq n$ as in the theorem, we can form the direct sum
	\[
	\alpha(M) := \bigoplus_{i = 1}^n \alpha_i(j^*_i(M)).
	\]
	Since a perverse sheaf $M$ is zero if and only if $j_i^*(M)$ is zero for all $1\leq i\leq n$, this functor is faithful. It is exact because the functor $j^*_i$ is exact for $1\leq i \leq n$. 
	
	Thus we may assume $X$ is affine. We can find a closed immersion $i\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^n$ for some $n \geq 0$ because $X$ is of finite type over $k$. We form the composite with the functor for $\mathbb{A}^n$ constructed in Theorem \ref{hypplanefunctor_THM}
	\[
	\textnormal{Perv}(X) \xrightarrow{i_*} \textnormal{Perv}(\mathbb{A}^n) \xrightarrow{\alpha_{n + 1}} \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell-\textnormal{fdVec}.
	\]
	Since $i_*$ and $\alpha_{n + 1}$ are exact, faithful, and $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-linear, the composite satisfies these conditions as well.

title: Lemma
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category and $N\colon M \rightarrow M$ a nilpotent endomorphism of an object $M \in \mathcal{A}$. Let $F\colon \mathcal{A}\rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ be an exact functor of abelian categories. The formation of the monodromy filtration commutes with $F$, i.e. we have
		\[
		F(\textnormal{Fil}^M_i(M)) = \textnormal{Fil}^M_i(F(M))
		\]
		and
		\[
		F(\textnormal{Gr}^M_i(M)) = \textnormal{Gr}^M_i(F(M)).
		\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the functor $F$ is exact, the formation of the graded commutes with $F$. Let $G^i(F(M))$ be the filtration on $F(M)$ induces by the monodromy filtration of $M$. The nilpotent operator $F(N)$ induces isomorphism
		\[
		F(N)^i\colon \textnormal{Gr}^G_{i}(F(M)) \rightarrow \textnormal{Gr}^G_{-i}(F(M)).
		\]
		for all $i \geq 0$. By uniqueness of the monodromy filtration (see \cite[Prop.~1.6.1]{DeligneWeilII}), we see that $G^i(F(M))$ is the monodromy filtration of $F(M)$.

label: tensorformula_PROP
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{tensorformula_PROP} Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category enriched over $K$-vector spaces. We assume $\mathcal{A}$ admits an exact and faithful $K$-linear functor
	\[
		\alpha\colon \mathcal{A} \rightarrow K-\textnormal{fdVec}.
	\]
	Let $M \in \mathcal{A}$ be an object with a nilpotent operator $N\colon M(1) \rightarrow M$. Let $V$ be a finite dimensional $K$-vector space with a nilpotent operator $N'\colon V(1) \rightarrow V$. We equip $M\otimes V$ with the monodromy operator $N\otimes 1 + 1\otimes N'$. The monodromy filtration is given by the tensor product formula
		\[
		\textnormal{Fil}^M_k(M\otimes V) = \sum_{i + j = k} \textnormal{Fil}^M_i(M)\otimes \textnormal{Fil}^M_j(V). 
		\]
		The graded pieces of the monodromy filtration satisfy 
		\[
		\textnormal{Gr}^M_k(M\otimes V) = \sum_{i + j = k} \textnormal{Gr}^M_i(M)\otimes \textnormal{Gr}^m_j(V). 
		\]
		Let $P_i, P'_j, P''_k$ be the primitive parts of the monodromy filtrations on $M$, $V$, and $M\otimes V$ respectively. Then we have
		\[
		P''_{k} = \bigoplus_{(i, j) \in I_k} P_{i}\otimes P'_{j} ({k - i - j}/{2}).
		\]
		where
		\[
		I_j := \big\{(j', j'') ~\big|~ {|j' - j''| \leq j \leq |j' + j''|,~ j \equiv j' + j''\textnormal{ mod }2}\big\}
		\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The formation of the monodromy filtration commutes with exact functors. Note that we have
		\[
		\alpha(M\otimes V) = \alpha(M)\otimes V
		\]
		because the functor is $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$-linear. Thus we may apply the tensor product formula of \cite[Prop.~1.6.9]{DeligneWeilII} to $\alpha(M\otimes V)$. One can now deduce the three claims because the functor is faithful and exact.
		
		Let us indicate how to prove that the monodromy filtration and the tensor product filtration agree. We are given two filtrations on $M\otimes V$ such that the induced filtrations on $\alpha(M\otimes V)$ agree. This implies that the filtrations of $M\otimes V$ are equal because the functor is faithful and exact. 
		
		To determine the graded pieces and the primitive parts, one can construct morphisms of objects in $\mathcal{A}$ and verify that they are isomorphisms by applying $\alpha$.

label: genbcprep_REM
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{genbcprep_REM}
	Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme. In the following theorems, we consider constructible complexes on $X$ over one of two base rings $R$. In the first case, $R$ is a Noetherian ring with an ideal $I \subset R$. We assume $R$ is complete with respect to the ideal $I$ and we equip $R$ with the $I$-adic topology. We also assume the kernel of the canonical morphism $\mathbb{Z} \rightarrow R$ is invertible on $X$.
	
	In the second case, we consider the ring $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$. In this case, we can write
	\[
	\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell = \varinjlim K
	\]  
	as a filtered colimit over finite extensions $K/\mathbb{Q}_\ell$. The fields $K$ are locally compact Hausdorff spaces and we equip $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ with the colimit topology. In both cases, a category of constructible complexes is constructed in \cite{hemo2023constructiblesheavesschemes}.
	
	We remark that  \cite[Prop.~5.2]{hemo2023constructiblesheavesschemes} and \cite[Cor.~2.4]{hansen2023relativeperversity} show that for each $K \in \textnormal{D}_c^b(X, \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell)$, there is a finite extension $K/\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$, and a complex $K_0 \in \textnormal{D}_c^b(X, \mathcal{O})$ with $K_0\otimes \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell = K$. This will allow us to reduce statements for the coefficient ring $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ to the Noetherian rings considered above. 
	
	In the first case, we remark that \cite[Prop.~7.6]{hemo2023constructiblesheavesschemes} and \cite[Prop.~6.1]{hemo2023constructiblesheavesschemes} show that the category of constructible complexes is equivalent to the category of constructible complexes constructed in \cite[Def.~6.5.1]{BhattSPE}. We will work primarily with the latter definition. 
		

	
	For the pushforward, we consider the pushforward in the proetale topology. For the pullback, we take the completed pullback defined as the $I$-derived completion of the pullback. For the ring $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$, we can utilize the equivalences \cite[Prop.~5.2]{hemo2023constructiblesheavesschemes} and \cite[Cor.~2.4]{hansen2023relativeperversity} to construct a completed pullback functor by localization.

title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathfrak{X}$ be a topos and $R \in \mathfrak{X}$ a ring object. For each $x \in \mathfrak{X}(R)$, we define the \textit{Koszul complex} $R(x)$ to be the cone of the morphism $$R \xrightarrow{x} R$$ of complexes concentrated in degree zero. For elements $x_1, \ldots,x_n \in \mathfrak{X}$, we define the Koszul complex to be the totalized tensor product
	\[
	R(x_1, \ldots, x_n) := R(x_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes R(x_n).
	\]
head: environment

label: koszulcom_REM
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{koszulcom_REM}
	Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $D$ a triangulated category enriched over $R$-modules. Let $x \in R$. For each $K \in D$, we can define $K\otimes R(x)$ to be the cone of the morphism
	\[
	K \xrightarrow{x} K \rightarrow K\otimes R(x) \xrightarrow{+}
	\]
	
	Let $F\colon D \rightarrow D'$ be an exact $R$-linear functor of triangulated categories enriched over $R$-modules. Note that we can find an isomorphism
	\[
	F(K\otimes R(x)) \cong F(K)\otimes R(x)
	\]
	for all $K \in D$ because the functor is exact and $R$-linear. In particular, if $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in R$ are elements, we can find an isomorphism
	\[
	F(K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots,x_n)) \cong F(K)\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)
	\]
	by induction on $n$. We see that tensoring by a Koszul complex commutes with any exact $R$-linear functor.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{genbcqcqs_REM}
	During the proofs of the following theorems, we need the generic base-change theorem, the generic universal local aciclicity theorem, and the generic constructibility theorem for the internal mapping object to hold for constructible etale sheaves over qcqs bases. We were only able to find the theorems over Noetherian schemes in the literature. One can reduce the case of qcqs bases to Noetherian bases by \cite[Cor.~2.7.4]{SGA4}. We give a detailed example of such a reduction during the proof of the generic universal local acyclicity theorem. We also give the reduction during the proof of the generic constructibility of the pushforward.

label: constlemma_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{constlemma_LEM}
	Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $R$ an Noetherian ring, complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$. Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X, R)$ be a bounded constructible complex of $R$-modules. Let $L \in \textnormal{D}^b_{\textnormal{coh}}(R)$ be a bounded complex with finite cohomology modules. We assume that the cohomology modules of $L$ are $I$-power torsion. The complex $K\otimes L$ is classical. Moreover, all cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes L$ are constructible.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The cohomology sheaves of the bounded complex $L$ are finitely generated $I$-power torsion modules. Since $L$ is bounded, the complex $L$ admits a finite filtration by complexes of the form $M'[e]$, where $M'$ is a $R/I$-module and $e \in \mathbb{Z}$. We have
	\[
	K\otimes_R M' = (K\otimes_R R/I)\otimes_{R/I} M'.
	\]
	Thus we see that $K\otimes_R M'$ is classical and the cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes_R M'$ are constructible. It follows from \cite[Cor.~5.1.9]{BhattSPE} and \cite[Prop.~5.2.9]{BhattSPE} that classical complexes are closed under cones for bounded below complexes. Since $K\otimes R/I$ is tor-finite, we obtain that all the terms $K\otimes_R M'$ are bounded. Thus $K\otimes_R L$ is classical.  Moreover, the cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes L$ are constructible because the category of constructible sheaves is closed under exact sequences.

title: Proof
body_md:
By Remark \ref{genbcprep_REM}, we may assume $R$ to be a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$. 
	
	The statement (2) requires a set of morphisms between pushforwards to be isomorphisms. The formation of these morphisms commutes with tensoring with the Koszul complex $R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ by Remark \ref{koszulcom_REM}. Moreover, the pushforward of an $I$-derived complete complex is always $I$-derived complete by \cite[Lem.~6.5.9]{BhattSPE}. Therefore, we may apply Nakayama's Lemma (see \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H83}{Tag 0H83}]{stacks-project}) to show the morphisms are isomorphism. Thus it is sufficient to verify the isomorphism after taking the derived tensor product with the Koszul complex. Thus we may pass to $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$. We remark that the cohomology sheaves of $K \otimes R(x_1, \ldots,x_n)$ are classical and constructible sheaves of $R/I$-modules by Lemma \ref{constlemma_LEM}. 
	
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
	
	For statement (2), the comparison isomorphism in \cite[Lem.~5.4.3]{BhattSPE} shows that the pushforward of the cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots,x_n)$ can be computed in the etale topology. Note that the completed pullback tensored with a Koszul complex reduces to an ordinary pullback tensored with a Koszul complex by definition of the completion functor. Therefore, the comparison isomorphism in \cite[Lem.~5.4.1]{BhattSPE} shows that the pullback can be computed in the etale topology. To prove that the pushforward commutes with base-change, it is therefore sufficient to prove that the pushforward of the cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots,x_n)$ commutes with base-change in the etale-topology.
	
	Thus we may assume $K$ is a constructible sheaf on the etale site of $X$. In this case, Noetherian approximation (see \cite[Cor.~2.7.4]{SGA4}) allows us to assume the sheaf descends to a base scheme $Y_0$ of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$. The property of satisfying base change is preserved by base change, so we may replace $Y$ by $Y_0$ and assume $Y$ is of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$. In this case, the existence of the stratification can be deduced from Noetherian induction and \cite[Ch.~7,~Cor.~2.9]{DeligneSGA45}.
		
	We turn to proving the statement (1). Our first step is to show that we have an isomorphism
	\[
	f_*(K)\otimes R/I \xrightarrow{\sim} f_*(K\otimes R/I).
	\] 
	Note that both sides of this morphism are $I$-derived complete complexes because they are annihilated by $I$. Thus it is sufficient if we show that
	\[
	(f_*(K)\otimes R/I) \otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \rightarrow f_*(K\otimes R/I)\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)
	\]
	is an isomorphism by Nakayama's Lemma. This morphism identifies with
	\[
	f_*(K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n))\otimes R/I \rightarrow f_*((K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n))\otimes R/I)
	\]
	by Remark \ref{koszulcom_REM}. Note that $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ is classical by Lemma \ref{constlemma_LEM}. Since we can compute the pushforward and the tensor product with $R/I$ in the etale topology, it is sufficient to show the isomorphism in the etale topology. In particular, it is sufficient if we show it over each geometric fiber of $X$ over $Y$ because the collection of all geometric points on $X$ is faithful in the etale topology. By (2), we may assume the formation of $f_*(K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n))$ and $f_*((K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n))\otimes R/I)$ commutes with base-change. In particular, we know the above morphism is an isomorphism over each geometric fiber of $X$ over $Y$ by \cite[Lem.~6.5.11~(3)]{BhattSPE}. Thus we obtain the desired isomorphism. 
	
	The isomorphism implies $f_*(K)\otimes R/I$ is classical. Therefore, it is sufficient if we show that the pushforward $f_*(K\otimes R/I)$, formed in the etale topology, is constructible. Point (2) and Noetherian approximation allow us to assume $Y$ is of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$. In this case, the reference \cite[Ch.~7,~Cor.~2.9]{DeligneSGA45} shows that the cohomology sheaves of $f_*(K\otimes R/I)$ are constructible. To prove that the complex $f_*(K\otimes R/I)$ is constructible, all that is left to show is that the stalks are perfect complexes. Since we may assume the formation of $f_*(K\otimes R/I)$ commutes with base-change, we may reduce to $Y$ a field. In this case, this follows from the discrete coefficient case over fields treated in \cite[Thm.~9.5.2]{LeiFu}.

label: genula_THM
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{genula_THM}
	Let $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a finitely presented morphism of qcqs schemes. We assume one of the following two conditions on the coefficient ring $R$:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The ring $R$ is Noetherian and complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$. We assume the characteristic of $R/I$ is invertible on $Y$.
		\item The ring $R$ is $R = \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_\ell$ for a prime $\ell$ invertible on $Y$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Let $K \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X, R)$. There exists a finite constructible partition
	\[
	Y = \bigsqcup_{i = 1}^n Y_i
	\]
	such that $K|_{Y_i}$ is universally locally acyclic over $Y_i$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We can assume $R$ is a Noetherian ring complete with respect to an ideal $I \subset R$ by Remark \ref{genbcprep_REM}. We denote by $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in I$ a set of generators of $I$. Note that the condition of being ULA involves a set of morphisms between cohomology groups of $I$-derived complete complexes on qcqs schemes being isomorphisms. Cohomology groups of an $I$-derived complete complex are $I$-derived complete by \cite[Lem.~6.5.9~(ii)]{BhattSPE}. By Nakayama's lemma (see \cite[\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H83}{Tag 0H83}]{stacks-project}) and Remark \ref{genbcqcqs_REM}, it is sufficient if we prove that such a partition exists for $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$. Note that the cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots,x_n)$ are constructible and classical by Lemma \ref{constlemma_LEM}. Thus we may assume $K$ is a classical constructible sheaf over a discrete coefficient ring with characteristic invertible on $Y$. The comparison isomorphism in \cite[Lem.~5.4.3]{BhattSPE} shows it is sufficient to show that the cohomology sheaves of $K\otimes R(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ are ULA over a constructible partition of $Y$ in the etale topology.
	
	In this case, Noetherian approximation (see \cite[Cor.~2.7.4]{SGA4}) allows us to assume the sheaf descends to a base scheme $Y_0$ of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$. Since the property of being ULA is, by definition, preserved by base-change, we may assume $Y$ is of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}[1/\ell]$. 
	
	In this case, Noetherian induction on $Y$ implies it is sufficient to prove that there exists a non-empty open subscheme of $Y$ over which $K$ is ULA. This statement is proven in \cite[Ch.~7,~Thm.~2.13]{DeligneSGA45}.

label: genbchom_THM
title: Theorem

title: Remark
body_md: Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete coefficient ring. We consider classical complexes $K, L \in \textnormal{D}(X, \Lambda)$ in the proetale topology on $X$. During the proof of the above theorem, we will utilize the classical internal mapping object. This is the internal mapping object of $K$ and $L$ formed in the etale topology and then sheafified in the proetale topology. We write $\textnormal{Hom}_{\Lambda, \textnormal{cl}}(K, L)$ for this object.
head: environment

label: genbcinternalhom_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{genbcinternalhom_LEM}
	Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $\Lambda$ a discrete Noetherian ring. Let $K, L, L' \in \textnormal{D}^b(X, \Lambda)$ be bounded classical complexes of $\Lambda$-modules on the proetale site of $X$. We assume $K$ is tor-finite. We have a natural isomorphism
	\[
	\textnormal{Hom}_{\Lambda}(K, \textnormal{Hom}_{\Lambda, \textnormal{cl}}(L, L')) = \textnormal{Hom}_{\Lambda}(K\otimes_{\Lambda} L, L')
	\]
	of objects in $\textnormal{D}(\Lambda)$.

label: genbchomcommutes_LEM
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{genbchomcommutes_LEM}
	Let $R$ be a complete Noetherian local ring. Let $f\colon X \rightarrow Y$ be a finitely presented morphism of qcqs schemes. Let $K, L \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X, R)$ be constructible complexes on $X$. Suppose the formation of $\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}})$ commutes with base change over $Y$. Let $n \geq m\geq 1$. We have
		\[
		\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^m = \textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^m, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^m, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^m).
		\]
	Moreover, the formation of 
	\[
	\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)
	\]
	commutes with base-change.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $n \geq 1$. We can filter $R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n$ by $R$-submodules isomorphic to $R/{\mathfrak{m}}$ because $R/{\mathfrak{m}}$ is a field. With this filtration, proving that the formation of the internal mapping object $\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)$ commutes with base-change can be reduced to proving that the formation of $\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}})$ commutes with base-change. We have an isomorphism
	\[
	\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}) = \textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}).
	\]
	
	To prove the coefficient formula, we note that the base-change implies we may assume $Y$ is a field. In this case, the statement is proven in the proof of \cite[Prop.~10.1.17]{LeiFu}

title: Proof
body_md:
By Remark \ref{genbcprep_REM}, we may assume $R$ is a complete Noetherian local ring.  We define 
	\[
	\textnormal{Hom}(K, L) := \varprojlim \textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n).
	\]
This object is well-defined by Lemma \ref{constlemma_LEM}. Moreover, it is ${\mathfrak{m}}$-derived complete because it is a limit of ${\mathfrak{m}}$-derived complete complexes. Let $K' \in \textnormal{D}^b_c(X, R)$ be a constructible complex. If $\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)$ is constructible, then Lemma \ref{genbcinternalhom_LEM} implies that we have isomorphisms 
\begin{align*}
	\textnormal{Hom}_R(K', \textnormal{Hom}(K, L)) &= \varprojlim \textnormal{Hom}_R(K', \textnormal{Hom}_{R/I^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/I^n, L\otimes R/I^n)) \\ 
	&= \varprojlim \textnormal{Hom}_{R/I^n}(K'\otimes R/I^n, \textnormal{Hom}_{R/I^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/I^n, L\otimes R/I^n)) \\
	                                                                                                                       
	                                                                                                                                  
	&= \varprojlim \textnormal{Hom}_{R/I^n}((K'\otimes_R R/I^n)\otimes_{R/I^n}(K \otimes_R R/I^n), L\otimes_R R/I^n)\\
	&= \varprojlim \textnormal{Hom}_{R/I^n}(K'\otimes_R K \otimes_R R/I^n, L\otimes R/I^n)\\
	&= \textnormal{Hom}_R(K'\otimes_R K, L) \\
\end{align*}
Therefore, if $\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)$ is constructible, then it is the internal mapping object of $K$ and $L$ in the category $\textnormal{D}^b_c(X, R)$. Our next step is to find a finite stratification of $Y$ over which the complexes are constructible. 

By \cite[Ch.~7,~Cor.~2.9]{DeligneSGA45} and Remark \ref{genbcqcqs_REM}, we may pass to a stratum in a stratification of $Y$ and assume that the formation of $\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}})$ commutes with base change in the etale topology. Since the pullback in the etale and the proetale topology are isomorphic by \cite[Lem.~5.4.1]{BhattSPE}, we see that the formation of the classical internal mapping object commutes with base-change in the proetale topology. Lemma \ref{genbchomcommutes_LEM} implies $$\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}} = \textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}})$$ and that the formation of 
\[
\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)
\]
commutes with base change for all $n \geq 1$.

By \cite[Ch.~7,~Cor.~2.9]{DeligneSGA45} and Remark \ref{genbcqcqs_REM}, we may pass to a further stratification to assume the complex $\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}})$ is constructible. This implies $\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)$ is constructible for all $n \geq 1$ by \cite[Lem.~6.3.12]{BhattSPE}. In particular, these complexes are bounded for all $n \geq 1$. 

Because these complexes are bounded and satisfy the above compatibility, \cite[Lem.~3.5.5]{BhattSPE} implies the isomorphism
\[
\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}} = \textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}). 
\]
This implies that the complex on the left is classical and constructible. Since $\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)$ is ${\mathfrak{m}}$-derived complete, it is a constructible complex. In particular, we obtain (1).

We now verify that the formation of the above complex commutes with base-change from the assumptions we imposed during the proof of (1). Let $g\colon Y' \rightarrow Y$ be a morphism of qcqs schemes. The reference \cite[Lem.~3.5.5]{BhattSPE} provides the isomorphism
\begin{align*}
	g^*_{\textnormal{}}(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L)) = \varprojlim g^*(\textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(K\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, L\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n)).
\end{align*}
The formation of the object on the right commutes with base-change, so we obtain
\[
g^*_{\textnormal{}}(\textnormal{Hom}(K, L))  = \varprojlim \textnormal{Hom}_{R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, \textnormal{cl}}(g^*(K)\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n, g^*(L)\otimes R/{\mathfrak{m}}^n).
\]
This is the construction above applied to $g^*(K)$ and $g^*(L)$. Note that the assumptions imposed during the proof of (1) are invariant under base change. Therefore, we may apply the same argument as above to show that this is the internal mapping object of $g^*(K)$ and $g^*(L)$ in the category of constructible complexes.
